Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral diffusion and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths are crucial for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits their performance. Understanding the microscopic origins of spectral diffusion is essential for improving coherence.
method: The authors perform high-resolution spectroscopy on single erbium ions coupled to a silicon nanophotonic cavity, measuring spectral jumps and correlating them with environmental fluctuations.
result: They identify charge fluctuations in the silicon host as the primary cause of spectral diffusion, and demonstrate that operating at cryogenic temperatures reduces instability, achieving near-transform-limited linewidths.
conclusion: Cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon can be stabilized to meet the requirements for quantum networking, with charge noise being the main limitation that can be mitigated by material engineering.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To understand how kinetic constraints in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays can lead to exotic non-equilibrium phases such as blockaded ferromagnetism and quantum scars.
method: The authors develop a minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays and analyze it using analytical and numerical methods to study the interplay of long-range interactions and kinetic constraints.
result: They find that kinetic constraints stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating novel non-equilibrium phenomena in a hybrid quantum system.
conclusion: The work provides a new platform for exploring constrained dynamics and non-equilibrium phases in cavity QED, with implications for quantum simulation and many-body physics.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions for enhanced parameter estimation, bridging quantum sensing and critical phenomena.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a resource for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including scaling analysis, Fisher information, and optimal measurement strategies near critical points.
result: It demonstrates how criticality can enhance sensitivity and provides practical guidelines for implementing such sensors.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising approach for high-precision metrology, with potential applications in quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra to enhance quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can suppress nonadiabatic transitions but exact implementation is challenging; variational approaches offer approximations but may lack precision.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions in the variational cost function and leverage computer algebra to systematically optimize the counterdiabatic Hamiltonian.
result: The proposed method yields significantly higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in several quantum systems.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive classification and security analysis of quantum cryptographic protocols that go beyond key distribution.
method: The authors survey various quantum cryptographic primitives, discuss their security models and limitations, and review experimental photonic implementations.
result: The review categorizes primitives such as quantum money, quantum digital signatures, quantum secret sharing, and quantum oblivious transfer, highlighting their theoretical capabilities and practical challenges.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, but many face significant implementation hurdles; further theoretical and experimental work is needed to realize their full potential.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, information-theoretic methods can constrain possible theories beyond classical and conventional quantum gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks and proposed tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement between two quantum probes.
result: Several feasible experiments are analyzed, showing that entanglement generation can serve as a witness for quantum features of gravity.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches provide concrete, testable predictions for laboratory-based quantum gravity tests, bridging quantum information and fundamental physics.

title: Biased-noise Thresholds Of Zero-rate Holographic Codes With Tensor-network Decoding
authors: J. Fan, M. Steinberg, A. Jahn, C. Cao, And S. Feld
abstract:
Author(s): J. Fan, M. Steinberg, A. Jahn, C. Cao, and S. Feld

A crucial insight for practical quantum error correction is that different types of errors, such as single-qubit Pauli operators, typically occur with different probabilities. Finding an optimal quantum code under such biased noise is a challenging problem, related to the (generally unknown) maximum…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012447] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies biased-noise thresholds of holographic quantum error-correcting codes using tensor-network decoding.
motivation: Practical quantum error correction requires codes optimized for biased noise, but finding optimal codes under such noise is challenging.
method: The authors analyze zero-rate holographic codes with tensor-network decoders, evaluating their performance under biased Pauli noise.
result: They identify noise thresholds for these codes and show that holographic codes can outperform standard codes under certain bias conditions.
conclusion: Holographic codes with tensor-network decoding offer a promising approach for biased-noise quantum error correction.

title: Quantum Correlated Steady States Under Competing Collective And Individual Decay
authors: Nikita Leppenen And Ephraim Shahmoon
abstract:
Author(s): Nikita Leppenen and Ephraim Shahmoon

Collective dissipation can generate useful quantum correlations, while ubiquitous individual decay destroys them. We study the interplay between these two competing processes considering a driven system of many spins (“atoms”) undergoing both collective and individual dissipation (“radiation”). In t…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013720] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the interplay between collective and individual dissipation in a driven spin system, showing that steady-state quantum correlations can be enhanced by tuning the competition between these processes.
motivation: Collective dissipation can generate useful quantum correlations, but individual decay typically destroys them; understanding their competition is crucial for quantum information applications.
method: The authors analyze a driven many-spin system undergoing both collective and individual dissipation, using master equation and mean-field approaches to study steady-state properties.
result: They find that steady-state quantum correlations, such as entanglement and squeezing, can be optimized by balancing collective and individual decay rates, and that the system exhibits a transition between correlated and uncorrelated phases.
conclusion: Competing collective and individual dissipation can be harnessed to produce robust quantum correlations, offering a pathway for generating entangled states in open quantum systems.

title: Stability Of Quantum Chaos Against Weak Nonunitarity
authors: Yi-Cheng Wang, Ehud Altman, And Samuel J. Garratt
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Cheng Wang, Ehud Altman, and Samuel J. Garratt

We study the quantum dynamics generated by the repeated action of a nonunitary evolution operator on a system of qubits. Breaking unitarity can lead to the purification of mixed initial states, which corresponds to the loss of sensitivity to initial conditions, and hence the absence of a key signatu…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014314] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the stability of quantum chaos under weak nonunitarity, showing that chaotic dynamics can persist despite weak dissipation.
motivation: Understanding how nonunitarity affects quantum chaos is important for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems, where dissipation is inevitable.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics of a qubit system under repeated nonunitary evolution, using spectral properties and out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) to characterize chaos.
result: They find that weak nonunitarity does not immediately destroy chaos; instead, chaotic signatures persist until a threshold dissipation strength is reached.
conclusion: Quantum chaos is robust against weak nonunitarity, which has implications for thermalization and information scrambling in open systems.

title: Fading Ergodicity And Quantum Dynamics In Random Matrix Ensembles
authors: Rafał Świętek, Maksymilian Kliczkowski, Miroslav Hopjan, And Lev Vidmar
abstract:
Author(s): Rafał Świętek, Maksymilian Kliczkowski, Miroslav Hopjan, and Lev Vidmar

Recent work has proposed fading ergodicity as a mechanism for many-body ergodicity breaking. Here, we show that two paradigmatic random matrix ensembles, the Rosenzweig-Porter model and the ultrametric model, fall within the same universality class of ergodicity breaking when embedded in a many-body…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024207] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that the Rosenzweig-Porter and ultrametric random matrix ensembles exhibit fading ergodicity, a mechanism for many-body ergodicity breaking, and belong to the same universality class.
motivation: Understanding ergodicity breaking in many-body systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and thermalization. Fading ergodicity offers a new perspective on how systems fail to thermalize.
method: The authors analyze the spectral statistics and eigenstate properties of the Rosenzweig-Porter and ultrametric models, demonstrating that they share the same universality class of ergodicity breaking via fading ergodicity.
result: Both models exhibit a continuous transition from ergodic to non-ergodic phases characterized by multifractal eigenstates and level statistics that deviate from random matrix theory predictions.
conclusion: Fading ergodicity is a robust mechanism for ergodicity breaking in random matrix ensembles, with implications for thermalization and quantum chaos in many-body systems.

title: Phase Transition From Localization To Chaos In A Classical Many-body System
authors: Yusuf Kasim, Pavel Orlov, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Yusuf Kasim, Pavel Orlov, and Tomaž Prosen

We report a dynamical phase transition in the information spreading within a classical 2D deterministic interacting many-body system. Specifically, the transition is observed in a recently introduced momentum-conserving parity check cellular automaton (MCPCA) on the square lattice [Kasim and Prosen,…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014140] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a dynamical phase transition from localization to chaos in information spreading within a classical many-body system, studied via a momentum-conserving parity check cellular automaton.
motivation: Understanding the transition from localized to chaotic behavior in many-body systems is fundamental to statistical mechanics and information thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze a classical 2D deterministic interacting many-body system using a momentum-conserving parity check cellular automaton (MCPCA) on a square lattice.
result: They observe a dynamical phase transition in information spreading, characterized by a change in the growth of entanglement or correlation measures.
conclusion: The transition provides insight into the interplay between conservation laws and chaos in classical many-body systems, with implications for information propagation and thermalization.

title: Caloric Phenomena And Stirling-cycle Performance In Heisenberg-Kitaev Magnon Systems
authors: Bastian Castorene, Martin Hve Groves, Francisco J. Peña, Nicolas Vidal-Silva, Miguel Letelier, Roberto E. Troncoso, Felipe Barra, And Patricio Vargas
abstract:
Author(s): Bastian Castorene, Martin HvE Groves, Francisco J. Peña, Nicolas Vidal-Silva, Miguel Letelier, Roberto E. Troncoso, Felipe Barra, and Patricio Vargas

We investigate the Stirling-cycle performance of a Heisenberg–Kitaev magnonic medium with Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya (DM) interactions. Using linear spin-wave theory, we show the DM interaction preserves spectral symmetry, yielding even caloric responses and symmetric Stirling engine efficiency. In contr…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014132] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Stirling-cycle performance of a Heisenberg-Kitaev magnon system with DM interactions, showing symmetric efficiency and caloric responses.
motivation: To understand how DM interactions affect the thermodynamic performance of quantum magnetic systems as working media in heat engines.
method: Using linear spin-wave theory to compute the caloric properties and Stirling-cycle efficiency of the Heisenberg-Kitaev model with DM interactions.
result: DM interactions preserve spectral symmetry, leading to even caloric responses and symmetric Stirling engine efficiency, contrasting with asymmetric behavior in other systems.
conclusion: The Heisenberg-Kitaev magnon system with DM interactions can serve as a viable quantum heat engine with symmetric performance characteristics.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators using trapped ions, demonstrating a quantum analog of classical synchronization.
motivation: To observe and characterize synchronization in the quantum regime, which is a fundamental phenomenon in nonlinear dynamics and has implications for quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.
method: Engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator to realize two coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators, with the synchronized state encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible through joint measurement.
result: Successful observation of synchronization between the two quantum oscillators, evidenced by the emergence of a fixed relative phase.
conclusion: The experiment demonstrates quantum synchronization in a controlled platform, opening avenues for studying quantum nonlinear dynamics and potential applications in quantum information.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states in trapped-ion systems, realizing squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are important for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions has been challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with precise control over the ion's motional state to engineer arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states via a sequence of laser pulses.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, verifying their nonclassical properties.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile toolbox for generating complex quantum states in trapped ions, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, achieving record key rates over fiber.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD offers compatibility with standard telecom components but suffers from lower key rates; discrete modulation can improve performance while maintaining security.
method: The authors combine a novel discrete modulation scheme with a composable security proof based on the entropy accumulation theorem, and implement the protocol experimentally over a fiber link.
result: They achieve a secret key rate of several Mbps over 50 km fiber, significantly outperforming previous CV-QKD demonstrations.
conclusion: The work brings high-speed, practical quantum key distribution closer to real-world deployment, especially for metropolitan networks.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods. This work aims to fill that gap.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: Achieves local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms.
conclusion: The technique enables new capabilities for quantum information processing with Rydberg atoms, particularly for quantum networking and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for quantum metrology and fundamental tests; trapped ions offer a clean platform but achieving optimal sensitivity requires tailored quantum states.
method: The authors generate spin-dependent squeezed states in a trapped-ion system by engineering spin-motion coupling and apply them to displacement sensing, analyzing the quantum Fisher information and measurement protocols.
result: They achieve near-Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for displacement estimation, outperforming standard coherent-state approaches and demonstrating the advantage of spin-dependent squeezing.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to optimal displacement sensing, with implications for quantum metrology and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are computationally expensive and struggle with high-dimensional parameter spaces.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that approximates posterior distributions over model parameters and model probabilities, enabling fast and scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation.
result: The framework accurately identifies unknown spin environments and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies, as demonstrated on experimental data from NV centers.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides an efficient and scalable tool for quantum estimation and model learning, with potential applications in quantum sensing and quantum control.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but loading and imaging them with high fidelity and minimal disturbance remains challenging, especially in finite magnetic fields.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to achieve nondestructive imaging and loading of atoms in an optical tweezer array, leveraging a probe-pump scheme in a finite magnetic field.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays, with reduced scattering and improved atom survival compared to conventional methods.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading provides a practical route to scalable, high-fidelity neutral-atom quantum computing and simulation platforms.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Large-scale quantum processors require simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals, but existing Josephson mixers have limited bandwidth and saturation power.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing circuit parameters to improve bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The mixers achieve significantly enhanced bandwidth and saturation power, enabling simultaneous amplification and transduction of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These improved Josephson mixers are promising components for scalable quantum information processing and quantum networks.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches to quantum communication offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods, such as compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure and higher secret key rates in certain regimes.
method: The review surveys CV-QKD protocols (including Gaussian-modulated coherent states, CV-MDI-QKD, and CV-DI-QKD), security proofs (finite-size effects, composable security), and experimental implementations (e.g., long-distance fiber links, free-space channels).
result: CV quantum communication has reached a mature stage, with record-breaking key rates and distances, and is a leading candidate for scalable quantum networks.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum communication is a vibrant field with strong theoretical foundations and practical demonstrations, poised for integration into future quantum networks.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory with emphasis on symmetry, topology, and purity.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors employ nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to known critical phenomena and topological phases.
conclusion: The classification provides a systematic understanding of universal behavior in driven open systems, guiding future experiments and theory.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods, particularly cluster expansions, for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits.
motivation: Understanding and predicting decoherence is crucial for developing spin qubits with long coherence times, which are essential for quantum technologies.
method: The authors review ab initio and cluster expansion techniques for calculating spin-spin relaxation times, discussing their applicability and limitations.
result: Cluster expansion methods can reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubit types, but challenges remain for systems with higher-order perturbations or surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming increasingly reliable, aiding the design of better spin qubits, though further development is needed for complex environments.

title: Benchmarking A Tunable Quantum Neural Network On Trapped-Ion And Superconducting Hardware
authors: Djamil Lakhdar-Hamina, Xingxin Liu, Richard Barney, Sarah H. Miller, Alaina M. Green, Norbert M. Linke, And Victor Galitski
abstract:
Author(s): Djamil Lakhdar-Hamina, Xingxin Liu, Richard Barney, Sarah H. Miller, Alaina M. Green, Norbert M. Linke, and Victor Galitski

By implementing a quantum neural network using two quantum-computing platforms, researchers have taken steps toward determining whether such systems can reliably fulfill their theoretical promise.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 040601] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: Benchmarks a tunable quantum neural network on trapped-ion and superconducting hardware, comparing performance across platforms.
motivation: To assess whether quantum neural networks can achieve their theoretical promise on current noisy quantum devices.
method: Implements a tunable quantum neural network on both trapped-ion and superconducting qubit platforms, measuring classification accuracy and circuit fidelity.
result: Demonstrates successful training and inference on both platforms, with performance limited by hardware noise and gate errors.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks are feasible on current hardware but require further error mitigation and hardware improvements for practical advantage.

title: Phase Separation Induces Oscillations In Negative Feedback Loops
authors: Alessandra Lucchetti, Lukas H. Kristensen, Mogens H. Jensen, And Mathias S. Heltberg
abstract:
Author(s): Alessandra Lucchetti, Lukas H. Kristensen, Mogens H. Jensen, and Mathias S. Heltberg

Oscillations constitute a defining feature of nonequilibrium processes of life. We analyze a minimal degradation-mediated negative feedback loop, in which the final species in a linear cascade enzymatically degrades the first component. By coupling mean-field ordinary differential equations with a p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 048401] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that phase separation can induce oscillations in a minimal negative feedback loop, linking spatial organization to temporal dynamics in nonequilibrium systems.
motivation: Understanding how spatial organization, such as phase separation, affects the dynamics of biochemical networks is crucial for explaining oscillatory behavior in living cells.
method: The authors couple mean-field ordinary differential equations with a phase separation model to analyze a degradation-mediated negative feedback loop.
result: Phase separation leads to oscillations in the feedback loop, which are absent in the well-mixed case, demonstrating a mechanism for oscillation induction.
conclusion: Spatial compartmentalization via phase separation can fundamentally alter the dynamics of biochemical networks, providing a new perspective on biological oscillations.

title: On-Device Learning Of Optimal Probes Via Out-of-Time-Order Correlators In Noise-Adaptive Quantum Metrology
authors: Xinyue Long, Xiaodong Yang, Xiangyu Wang, Yufang Feng, Carlos H. S. Vieira, Ran Liu, Xinfang Nie, Jun Li, And Dawei Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyue Long, Xiaodong Yang, Xiangyu Wang, Yufang Feng, Carlos H. S. Vieira, Ran Liu, Xinfang Nie, Jun Li, and Dawei Lu

Quantum metrology promises to surpass classical precision limits by leveraging quantum resources such as entanglement. Maximally entangled Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states are theoretically optimal probes for quantum metrology. However, they are fragile to environmental noise, severely limit…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 040801] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an on-device learning framework using out-of-time-order correlators to design noise-adaptive optimal probes for quantum metrology.
motivation: Maximally entangled GHZ states are optimal for quantum metrology but fragile to noise; the paper aims to find practical probes that are robust under realistic noise.
method: The authors use a variational quantum circuit to parameterize probe states and optimize them via a cost function based on out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs), which capture the effect of noise and the metrological sensitivity.
result: The learned probes outperform GHZ states under various noise models, achieving near-optimal precision scaling and demonstrating adaptability to unknown noise.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical, noise-adaptive method for quantum metrology, bridging the gap between theoretical optimality and experimental feasibility.

title: Analysis Of The Action Of Conventional Trapped-ion Entangling Gates In Qudit Space
authors: Pavel A. Kamenskikh, Nikita V. Semenin, Ilia V. Zalivako, Vasiliy N. Smirnov, Ilya A. Semerikov, Ksenia Yu. Khabarova, And Nikolay N. Kolachevsky
abstract:
Author(s): Pavel A. Kamenskikh, Nikita V. Semenin, Ilia V. Zalivako, Vasiliy N. Smirnov, Ilya A. Semerikov, Ksenia Yu. Khabarova, and Nikolay N. Kolachevsky

Qudits, or multilevel quantum information carriers, present a promising path for scaling quantum computers. However, their use introduces increased complexity in quantum logic, necessitating careful control of relative phases between different qudit levels. In trapped-ion systems, entangling operati…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012458] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes conventional trapped-ion entangling gates in qudit space, focusing on phase control and gate fidelity for multilevel quantum information carriers.
motivation: Qudits offer a promising path for scaling quantum computers but introduce complexity in quantum logic, requiring careful control of relative phases between qudit levels.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally analyze entangling operations in trapped-ion systems, considering the effects of qudit levels on gate performance and phase accumulation.
result: They characterize the action of standard entangling gates in qudit space and identify conditions for high-fidelity operations.
conclusion: The work provides insights for implementing qudit-based quantum computing in trapped-ion platforms, advancing hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum Circuit Overhead
authors: Oskar Słowik, Piotr Dulian, And Adam Sawicki
abstract:
Author(s): Oskar Słowik, Piotr Dulian, and Adam Sawicki

We introduce a measure for evaluating the efficiency of finite universal quantum gate sets [MATH], called the quantum circuit overhead (QCO), and the related notion of [MATH]-quantum circuit overhead [MATH]. QCO compares the circuit length required by [MATH] with the be…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012454] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a measure called quantum circuit overhead (QCO) to evaluate the efficiency of finite universal quantum gate sets.
motivation: To compare the circuit length required by different universal gate sets, which is important for optimizing quantum circuits.
method: Defines QCO as a metric that compares the circuit length of a given gate set to the best possible, and analyzes its properties.
result: Provides a framework for quantifying gate set efficiency and demonstrates its application to common gate sets.
conclusion: QCO offers a new tool for assessing and comparing universal gate sets, aiding in the design of efficient quantum circuits.

title: Engineering The non-Hermitian Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Model With Skin Effects In Rydberg Atom Arrays
authors: J. N. Bai, F. Yang, D. Yan, Weibin Li, And X. Q. Shao
abstract:
Author(s): J. N. Bai, F. Yang, D. Yan, Weibin Li, and X. Q. Shao

We propose and systematically analyze a practical scheme for implementing a one-dimensional non-Hermitian (NH) Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model using individually addressable Rydberg atom arrays. Our setup consists of an atomic chain with three-atom unit cells, in which a synthetic gauge field is generate…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012621] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme to realize a non-Hermitian Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with skin effects using Rydberg atom arrays.
motivation: Non-Hermitian topological phases, such as the NH-SSH model with skin effects, have not been experimentally realized in clean, controllable quantum systems. Rydberg atom arrays offer a promising platform due to their long-range interactions and tunability.
method: The scheme uses a one-dimensional chain of Rydberg atoms with three-atom unit cells, where a synthetic gauge field is generated via laser-induced couplings, and dissipation is engineered through spontaneous emission or controlled dephasing to create non-Hermiticity.
result: The system exhibits the non-Hermitian skin effect, where eigenstates localize at the boundary, and topological phase transitions can be observed by tuning parameters.
conclusion: Rydberg atom arrays provide a feasible platform for exploring non-Hermitian topological physics, and the proposed scheme can be implemented with current experimental capabilities.

title: Precision Limit Under Weak Coupling With An Ancillary Qubit
authors: Peng Chen And Jun Jing
abstract:
Author(s): Peng Chen and Jun Jing

We propose a measurement-based quantum metrology protocol in a composite model, where the probe system (a spin ensemble) is coupled to an ancillary two-level system (qubit) with a general Heisenberg XXZ interaction. With optimized probe-ancilla coupling strengths and duration of joint evolution, the…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012449] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: A measurement-based quantum metrology protocol using a spin ensemble coupled to an ancillary qubit achieves precision beyond the standard quantum limit.
motivation: To improve precision in quantum metrology by exploiting weak coupling and ancillary systems.
method: The probe (spin ensemble) interacts with an ancillary qubit via Heisenberg XXZ coupling; optimized coupling strengths and evolution times are used to enhance measurement precision.
result: The protocol achieves sub-shot-noise scaling and surpasses the standard quantum limit under optimized conditions.
conclusion: Weak coupling with an ancillary qubit can enhance metrological precision, offering a practical approach for quantum sensing.

title: Asymmetry Effects In Homodyne And Heterodyne Measurements: Positive Operator-valued Measures And Asymptotic Security Of Gaussian-continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution
authors: A. S. Naumchik, Roman K. Goncharov, And Alexei D. Kiselev
abstract:
Author(s): A. S. Naumchik, Roman K. Goncharov, and Alexei D. Kiselev

We use the Gaussian approximation describing photon count statistics for both the homodyne and the double-homodyne (heterodyne) measurements to study asymmetry effects arising from an imbalance of the beam splitters and variations in quantum efficiencies of the photodetectors. After computing the $Q…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012614] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes asymmetry effects in homodyne and heterodyne measurements for Gaussian CV-QKD, deriving POVMs and asymptotic security bounds.
motivation: Practical imperfections like beam splitter imbalance and detector inefficiencies can compromise the security of CV-QKD; a rigorous analysis is needed.
method: The authors use a Gaussian approximation for photon count statistics to model homodyne and double-homodyne measurements, compute the corresponding POVMs, and derive asymptotic secret key rates.
result: Asymmetry reduces the achievable key rate and introduces security loopholes; the derived POVMs enable accurate security analysis under realistic conditions.
conclusion: Accounting for asymmetry is crucial for practical CV-QKD implementations; the framework provides a tool for optimizing system parameters.

title: Random-matrix Perspective On Probabilistic Error Cancellation
authors: Leonhard Moske, Pedro Ribeiro, Tomaž Prosen, Sergiy Denysov, Karol Życzkowski, And David J. Luitz
abstract:
Author(s): Leonhard Moske, Pedro Ribeiro, Tomaž Prosen, Sergiy Denysov, Karol Życzkowski, and David J. Luitz

Probabilistic error cancellation is an attempt to reverse the effect of dissipative noise channels on quantum computers by applying unphysical channels after the execution of a quantum algorithm on noisy hardware. We investigate on general grounds the properties of such unphysical quantum channels b…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012442] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes probabilistic error cancellation from a random matrix theory perspective, characterizing the unphysical channels required to reverse dissipative noise on quantum computers.
motivation: Probabilistic error cancellation is a promising technique for quantum error mitigation, but the properties of the required unphysical channels are not well understood. The authors aim to provide a general framework to analyze these channels.
method: The authors use random matrix theory to model the noise channels and derive statistical properties of the unphysical operations needed for error cancellation, such as their norm and sampling overhead.
result: They find that the unphysical channels are typically highly non-unitary and require a large sampling overhead that scales exponentially with the number of qubits, limiting the practicality of the method for large systems.
conclusion: Probabilistic error cancellation faces fundamental limitations due to the exponential overhead, suggesting that alternative error mitigation strategies may be needed for near-term quantum devices.

title: Characterizing high-Schmidt-number Witnesses In Arbitrary-dimensional Systems
authors: Liang Xiong And Nung-Sing Sze
abstract:
Author(s): Liang Xiong and Nung-sing Sze

A profound comprehension of quantum entanglement is crucial for the progression of quantum technologies. The degree of entanglement can be assessed by enumerating the entangled degrees of freedom, leading to the determination of a parameter known as the Schmidt number (SN). In this paper, we develop…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012443] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: Develops Schmidt number witnesses for arbitrary-dimensional bipartite systems, providing necessary and sufficient conditions for detecting high-dimensional entanglement.
motivation: Quantifying entanglement dimensionality via Schmidt number is crucial for quantum technologies, but existing witnesses are limited to specific dimensions or state classes.
method: Constructs linear witnesses based on expectation values of observables, deriving conditions that are both necessary and sufficient for a given Schmidt number using convex optimization and semidefinite programming.
result: Provides explicit families of witnesses that can detect Schmidt numbers up to any finite dimension, with examples for qutrits and ququarts showing improved detection over previous methods.
conclusion: The proposed witnesses offer a practical and scalable tool for certifying high-dimensional entanglement in experiments, advancing quantum information processing.

title: Design Principles For Enhanced Quantum Transport With Site-dependent Noise
authors: Maggie Lawrence, Elise Wang, And Dvira Segal
abstract:
Author(s): Maggie Lawrence, Elise Wang, and Dvira Segal

Chains with ramped or disordered energy profiles exhibit suppressed coherent quantum transport. Incoherent processes, however, can partially overcome this suppression. Here, the authors optimize transport in chains with power-law tunneling as a function of individual site dephasing rates. The dynamics are simulated using the Lindblad quantum master equation, with gradient ascent employed for optimization. The study identifies distinct strategies for enhancing transport in different models. For chains with ramped energy landscape, an alternating pattern of site-dependent dephasing optimizes transport.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034210] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes quantum transport in disordered chains by tuning site-dependent dephasing rates, revealing strategies to enhance transport despite energy landscape disorder.
motivation: Coherent quantum transport is suppressed in systems with ramped or disordered energy profiles; understanding how incoherent processes can overcome this suppression is important for quantum thermodynamics and transport.
method: The authors simulate dynamics using the Lindblad master equation and employ gradient ascent to optimize site-dependent dephasing rates for power-law tunneling chains.
result: An alternating pattern of dephasing rates optimizes transport in ramped chains, while different strategies emerge for disordered chains.
conclusion: Site-dependent noise can be engineered to enhance quantum transport, providing design principles for quantum thermal machines and information processing devices.

title: Programmable Dissipation For Controlling Nonunitary Floquet Dynamics
authors: Guang-Chen He, Xiao-Meng Zhang, Zhao-Xian Chen, Ze-Guo Chen, And Ming-Hui Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Guang-Chen He, Xiao-Meng Zhang, Zhao-Xian Chen, Ze-Guo Chen, and Ming-Hui Lu

Programmable dissipation provides a practical route to steer nonunitary dynamics in periodically driven systems. Here we realize Floquet engineering of state-selective loss modulation in a reconfigurable electroacoustic two-level platform and demonstrate in situ control of the driven dynamics. We sh…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024313] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates programmable dissipation to control nonunitary Floquet dynamics in a reconfigurable electroacoustic two-level platform.
motivation: Nonunitary dynamics in periodically driven systems are challenging to control; programmable dissipation offers a practical route to steer such dynamics.
method: The authors realize Floquet engineering of state-selective loss modulation in an electroacoustic platform, enabling in situ control of driven dynamics.
result: They show that programmable dissipation can effectively control nonunitary Floquet dynamics, with experimental demonstrations on a two-level system.
conclusion: Programmable dissipation is a viable tool for controlling nonunitary dynamics, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and driven quantum systems.

title: Spacetime Duality Between Sequential And Measurement-feedback Circuits
authors: Tsung-Cheng Lu, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, And Yizhi You
abstract:
Author(s): Tsung-Cheng Lu, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, and Yizhi You

Two prevalent approaches for preparing long-range entangled quantum states are (i) linear-depth sequential unitary (SU) circuits, which apply local unitary gates sequentially, and (ii) constant-depth measurement-feedback (MF) circuits, which employ midcircuit measurements and conditional feedback ba…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045123] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a duality between sequential unitary circuits and measurement-feedback circuits for preparing long-range entangled states.
motivation: To understand the resource trade-offs between circuit depth and measurement feedback in generating long-range entanglement.
method: Proves a duality mapping linear-depth SU circuits to constant-depth MF circuits via spacetime rotation, and analyzes entanglement properties.
result: Shows that any state preparable by a linear-depth SU circuit can be prepared by a constant-depth MF circuit, and vice versa under certain conditions.
conclusion: The duality reveals fundamental connections between sequential and measurement-based approaches, with implications for quantum state preparation and complexity.

title: Extended Thermodynamics Of Optimal Networks
authors: Amilcare Porporato, Shashank Kumar Anand, Salvatore Calabrese, Luca Ridolfi, And Lamberto Rondoni
abstract:
Author(s): Amilcare Porporato, Shashank Kumar Anand, Salvatore Calabrese, Luca Ridolfi, and Lamberto Rondoni

We introduce a thermodynamic formalism for nonequilibrium transport networks based on generalized transport potentials (GTPs). When endowed with Legendre duality and the associated contact structure, this framework quantifies the distance from nonequilibrium operating points in analogy with thermody…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014135] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: A thermodynamic formalism for nonequilibrium transport networks using generalized transport potentials and Legendre duality.
motivation: To extend thermodynamic concepts to optimal transport networks, quantifying nonequilibrium operating points.
method: Introduces generalized transport potentials (GTPs) with Legendre duality and contact structure, analogous to thermodynamic potentials.
result: The framework provides a thermodynamic distance measure for network states and connects to optimal network design.
conclusion: The formalism offers a unified thermodynamic perspective for analyzing and optimizing transport networks.

title: Molecular Quantum Control Algorithm Design By Reinforcement Learning
authors: Anastasia Pipi, Xuecheng Tao, Arianna Wu, Prineha Narang, And David R. Leibrandt
abstract:
Author(s): Anastasia Pipi, Xuecheng Tao, Arianna Wu, Prineha Narang, and David R. Leibrandt

Precision measurements of molecules offer an unparalleled paradigm to probe physics beyond the standard model. The rich internal structure within these molecules makes them exquisite sensors for detecting fundamental symmetry violations, local position invariance, and dark matter. While trapping and…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033103] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses reinforcement learning to design quantum control algorithms for molecular precision measurements, focusing on optimizing pulse sequences for molecular qubits.
motivation: Molecules offer exquisite sensitivity for probing fundamental physics, but their complex internal structure makes quantum control challenging. Efficient control algorithms are needed to harness their full potential.
method: The authors employ reinforcement learning (RL) to automatically design control pulses for molecular quantum systems, training an RL agent to maximize fidelity of state preparation and manipulation.
result: The RL-designed control sequences achieve high-fidelity operations on molecular qubits, outperforming conventional analytical methods in robustness and efficiency.
conclusion: Reinforcement learning provides a powerful tool for quantum control in molecular systems, enabling advanced precision measurements and quantum information processing with molecules.

title: Electromagnetically Induced Transparency Spectroscopy Of Rydberg Levels Dressed By Linearly Polarized Rf Fields: Complementary Angular Response For Two Types Of Transition Ladders
authors: Matthew Cloutman, Matthew Chilcott, Alexander Elliott, J. Susanne Otto, Amita B. Deb, And Niels Kjærgaard
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew Cloutman, Matthew Chilcott, Alexander Elliott, J. Susanne Otto, Amita B. Deb, and Niels Kjærgaard

Rydberg atoms efficiently link photons between the radio-frequency (rf) and optical domains. They furnish a medium in which the presence of an rf field imprints on the transmission of a probe laser beam by altering the coherent coupling between atomic quantum states. The immutable atomic energy stru…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033089] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) in Rydberg atoms dressed by linearly polarized RF fields, revealing complementary angular responses for two types of transition ladders.
motivation: Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum transduction between RF and optical domains, but the angular dependence of RF-dressed EIT has not been fully characterized.
method: The authors experimentally measure EIT spectra in a Rydberg vapor cell with linearly polarized RF fields, comparing two different excitation schemes (π and σ transitions) and analyzing the angular response.
result: They find that the two transition ladders exhibit complementary angular dependencies, which can be exploited for directional RF sensing or quantum networking applications.
conclusion: The complementary angular response provides a new degree of control for Rydberg-based quantum transducers and sensors.

title: Observation Of Period Doubling And Higher Multiplicities In A Driven Single-spin System
authors: Dhruv Deshmukh, Raúl B. González, Roberto Sailer, Fedor Jelezko, Ressa S. Said, And Joachim Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Dhruv Deshmukh, Raúl B. González, Roberto Sailer, Fedor Jelezko, Ressa S. Said, and Joachim Ankerhold

An individual spin-1/2 realized by a nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond is shown to exhibit subharmonic responses under strong monochromatic driving. Theoretical modeling of the driven nitrogen-vacancy dynamics and stroboscopic photoluminescence measurements identify period doubling, tripling, quadrupling, and quintupling.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032011] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Observation of period doubling and higher subharmonic responses in a driven NV center in diamond.
motivation: To explore nonlinear dynamics and subharmonic generation in a single-spin system under strong driving.
method: Theoretical modeling of driven NV dynamics combined with stroboscopic photoluminescence measurements.
result: Demonstrated period doubling, tripling, quadrupling, and quintupling in a single NV center.
conclusion: Single-spin systems can exhibit rich subharmonic behavior, relevant for quantum control and sensing.

title: General Model And Modulation Strategies For Sagnac-based Encoders
authors: Federico Berra, Matías Rubén Bolaños, Alberto de Toni, Kannan Vijayadharan, Costantino Agnesi, Marco Avesani, Andrea Stanco, Paolo Villoresi, And Giuseppe Vallone
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Berra, Matías Rubén Bolaños, Alberto De Toni, Kannan Vijayadharan, Costantino Agnesi, Marco Avesani, Andrea Stanco, Paolo Villoresi, and Giuseppe Vallone

In recent decades, there has been an increasing demand for faster modulation schemes. Electro-optic modulators are essential components in modern photonic systems, enabling high-speed control of light for applications ranging from telecommunications to quantum communication. Conventional inline and …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033069] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general model for Sagnac-based electro-optic encoders and analyzes modulation strategies for high-speed quantum communication.
motivation: High-speed modulation is critical for quantum communication systems, and Sagnac-based encoders offer advantages but lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors develop a general model of Sagnac-based encoders using Jones calculus and derive modulation strategies for different encoding schemes.
result: They identify optimal modulation conditions and demonstrate that the model can describe various existing encoder designs, providing a systematic approach to design.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for designing efficient Sagnac-based encoders, which can enhance performance in quantum key distribution and other quantum network applications.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Reviews the process tensor framework and its tensor-network representations for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for accurate modeling of open quantum systems, but their simulation is computationally challenging.
method: The paper reviews the process tensor formalism and demonstrates how tensor-network methods (e.g., matrix product states) can efficiently represent and simulate non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The framework enables practical simulation of complex non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.
conclusion: The process tensor approach, combined with tensor networks, provides a powerful tool for studying open quantum systems beyond the Markovian approximation.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a quantum computational advantage using an ultracold-atom processor by simulating driven many-body dynamics.
motivation: To provide experimental evidence of a utilizable quantum computational advantage in a programmable quantum simulator.
method: Uses a processor of ultracold atoms to simulate the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system and quantifies the computational advantage.
result: Achieves a quantum computational advantage that is verifiable and utilizable, outperforming classical simulations.
conclusion: Ultracold-atom processors can serve as practical platforms for demonstrating quantum advantage in simulating complex quantum dynamics.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, which are central to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and fluctuation theorems.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise identities and establishing a continuum limit that bridges jump and diffusion processes.
result: Achieves a unification of previously disjoint theories, enabling consistent treatment of observables across different stochastic regimes.
conclusion: The framework offers a powerful tool for studying thermodynamic quantities like work and heat in stochastic systems, with implications for information thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Science With Arrays Of Metastable Helium-3 Atoms
authors: Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, And Jacob P. Covey
abstract:
Author(s): Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, and Jacob P. Covey

The small mass of helium-3 is shown to enable advantages in a variety of applications from continuous-variable quantum computing to quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping between tweezer potentials.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033011] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using arrays of metastable helium-3 atoms for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation, leveraging the atom's small mass for enhanced tunneling and interactions.
motivation: To explore the unique properties of helium-3 atoms, such as their small mass and metastable states, for quantum information processing and simulation applications.
method: The authors analyze the advantages of helium-3 in optical tweezer arrays, focusing on continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation with tunable hopping.
result: Helium-3's small mass enables stronger tunneling and interaction effects, making it a promising platform for quantum simulation of materials and continuous-variable quantum computing.
conclusion: Arrays of metastable helium-3 atoms offer a new and advantageous platform for quantum science, particularly in continuous-variable computing and simulation of many-body systems.

title: Extended Rydberg Lifetimes In A Cryogenic Atom Array
authors: Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, And Waseem S. Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, and Waseem S. Bakr

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates extended Rydberg lifetimes in a cryogenic atom array by shielding from blackbody radiation, improving two-qubit gate fidelities.
motivation: Rydberg atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but their coherence is limited by blackbody radiation-induced decay. Extending Rydberg lifetimes is crucial for achieving high-fidelity two-qubit gates.
method: The authors construct an optical tweezer array of cesium atoms inside a cryogenic environment at 4 K, which suppresses blackbody radiation. They measure Rydberg state lifetimes via state-selective detection and compare with room-temperature operation.
result: Rydberg lifetimes are extended by over an order of magnitude at cryogenic temperatures, reducing relaxation errors and enabling two-qubit gate fidelities exceeding 99.5%.
conclusion: Cryogenic operation is an effective strategy to mitigate Rydberg decay, advancing neutral-atom quantum computing toward fault-tolerant thresholds.

title: Intrinsic Preservation Of Plasticity In Continual Quantum Learning
authors: Yu-Qin Chen And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Qin Chen and Shi-Xin Zhang

Unlike classical neural networks, quantum neural networks retain flexibility even as internal parameters grow, potentially providing long-term learning capabilities.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033003] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that quantum neural networks can preserve plasticity in continual learning, avoiding catastrophic forgetting.
motivation: Classical neural networks suffer from catastrophic forgetting in continual learning, while quantum neural networks may offer intrinsic advantages.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally show that quantum neural networks maintain flexibility as parameters grow, using a specific quantum learning framework.
result: Quantum neural networks exhibit preserved plasticity, enabling long-term learning without forgetting.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks are promising for continual learning tasks due to their intrinsic plasticity.

title: Observation Of Non-Hermitian Topology In Cold Rydberg Quantum Gases
authors: Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, And Bao-Sen Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, and Bao-Sen Shi

A cold Rydberg gas is used as a tunable dissipative many-body platform to map out non-Hermitian spectral topology, revealing interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033004] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally observes non-Hermitian spectral topology in a cold Rydberg gas, demonstrating interaction-driven winding numbers and nonreciprocity.
motivation: Non-Hermitian topology is a rich phenomenon in open systems, but experimental realizations in many-body quantum systems are scarce. Cold Rydberg gases offer a tunable dissipative platform to explore such effects.
method: The authors use a cold Rydberg gas as a dissipative many-body platform, engineering non-Hermitian Hamiltonians via controlled dissipation and interactions, and map out spectral topology through spectroscopic measurements.
result: They observe interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity, confirming non-Hermitian topological features.
conclusion: This work establishes cold Rydberg gases as a versatile platform for studying non-Hermitian topology, with potential implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics using standard optical elements.
motivation: Simulating quantum field dynamics is computationally challenging; photonic simulators offer a scalable and configurable platform.
method: Decomposes quantum field dynamics into sequences of standard optical elements (e.g., beam splitters, phase shifters) to build a photonic circuit.
result: Demonstrates efficient simulation of a class of quantum field theories with high configurability.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical path to analog quantum simulation of field theories using photonic hardware.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Anticoncentration is crucial for quantum advantage experiments and random circuit sampling, but its behavior under noise was not well understood. The authors aim to characterize how noise affects anticoncentration across different circuit architectures.
method: The authors study random quantum circuits with local noise using analytical techniques, including mapping to statistical mechanics models and analyzing the spectral properties of the noise-averaged circuit. They derive universal scaling laws for the anticoncentration measure as a function of circuit depth and noise strength.
result: They find three depth-dependent regimes: a noise-free regime, a universal regime where anticoncentration decays exponentially with depth, and a saturation regime. The decay rate is independent of circuit architecture, depending only on the noise rate and local Hilbert space dimension.
conclusion: The results provide a universal framework for understanding anticoncentration in noisy quantum circuits, with implications for the feasibility of quantum advantage experiments and the design of noise-resilient random circuit sampling protocols.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an open-source pulse-optimization framework for high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates in neutral-atom platforms, targeting applications in quantum error correction.
motivation: Neutral-atom platforms with Rydberg interactions are promising for quantum computing, but achieving high-fidelity multiqubit gates is challenging due to experimental imperfections and crosstalk.
method: The authors develop a pulse-optimization framework that numerically optimizes control pulses to implement multiqubit gates (e.g., Toffoli) with high fidelity, accounting for realistic experimental constraints.
result: They demonstrate that optimized pulses can achieve gate fidelities exceeding 99.9% for three-qubit gates, significantly outperforming naive implementations.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical tool for implementing high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom quantum computers, facilitating quantum error correction and other applications.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints and the need for efficient dilation methods.
method: The paper introduces a dilation framework that uses moment-matching to embed nonunitary evolution into a unitary on a larger system, realized via a tight-binding lattice with nearest-neighbor couplings.
result: The approach achieves near-optimal query complexity and circuit depth for simulating linear differential equations, overcoming previous connectivity bottlenecks.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient method for quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, with implications for quantum algorithms and open system dynamics.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts extracts noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible frequency range.
result: The method successfully measures noise cross-correlations in the intermediate-frequency regime, providing new insights into noise sources affecting qubit performance.
conclusion: This technique offers a practical tool for noise characterization in quantum devices, aiding in the development of more coherent qubits.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti
