Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. This work explores collective effects to achieve blockade with weaker coupling.
method: The authors theoretically analyze an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, deriving conditions for photon blockade and studying the dependence on system size.
result: They find that photon blockade strengthens with increasing ensemble size, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission even when single-emitter coupling is weak.
conclusion: Collective enhancement offers a practical route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum information processing with light.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Fourier neural operators are used to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of periodically driven quantum systems, enabling extrapolation beyond training data.
motivation: Modeling time-periodic quantum systems is computationally challenging; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations and predict long-time behavior.
method: The authors employ Fourier neural operators that learn mappings in frequency space, trained on time-series data of observables or states, to approximate the Floquet Hamiltonian and time evolution.
result: The method accurately reproduces Floquet Hamiltonians and observable dynamics, and generalizes to unseen driving periods and longer times, demonstrating operator growth learning.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a powerful tool for studying periodically driven quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique using classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise, with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling is essential for protecting quantum information from noise, but existing methods are inefficient for spatially correlated noise. This work aims to design efficient, device-tailored sequences.
method: The authors map the problem of designing dynamical decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, leveraging error correction principles to cancel k-local noise.
result: They produce sequences whose length scales independently of the number of qubits, enabling practical implementation for large quantum systems.
conclusion: This approach bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering a scalable solution for noise mitigation in quantum devices.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A colloquium review that provides a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian dynamics in open quantum systems, covering methods across quantum optics, thermodynamics, and solid-state physics.
motivation: Open quantum systems are crucial for quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate; a unified overview of methods is needed.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and review various simulation techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The paper systematically compares different methods, highlighting their commonalities and differences, and provides guidance on choosing appropriate techniques for specific problems.
conclusion: The unified framework clarifies the relationships among diverse simulation methods and offers a practical guide for researchers working on non-Markovian open quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in gate simplification and experimental feasibility.
motivation: Qubits are standard for quantum computing, but qudits may offer resource-efficient alternatives for certain tasks, such as simplifying the Toffoli gate. This review surveys the potential roles of qudits in quantum information processing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical embeddings of qudits into qubit systems, gate decomposition techniques using qudits, and experimental implementations across various platforms (e.g., trapped ions, superconducting circuits).
result: Qudits can reduce the number of elementary operations for multiqubit gates (e.g., Toffoli gate with a qutrit) and enable more efficient quantum algorithms. Experimental progress is summarized, showing proof-of-principle demonstrations.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for quantum computing, offering trade-offs between qubit count and gate complexity, but further development in qudit control and error correction is needed for practical advantage.

title: Scalable High-fidelity And Near-deterministic Preparation Of Large-photon-number States
authors: Mo Xiong, Jize Han, Chuanzhen Cao, Jinbin Li, Zhiguo Huang, And Ming Xue
abstract:
Author(s): Mo Xiong, Jize Han, Chuanzhen Cao, Jinbin Li, Zhiguo Huang, and Ming Xue

The scalable preparation of large photon-number (Fock) states is a long-standing frontier in quantum science, with direct implications for quantum metrology and bosonic quantum information processing. Despite substantial progress at small photon numbers, extending state generation to large photon nu…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013721] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: A scalable method for preparing large-photon-number Fock states with high fidelity and near-deterministic success.
motivation: Large Fock states are essential for quantum metrology and bosonic quantum information processing, but existing methods are limited to small photon numbers.
method: The authors propose a protocol using a cascaded array of nonlinear optical elements and photon-number-resolving detectors to sequentially add photons to a state.
result: The scheme achieves near-deterministic generation of Fock states with up to 10 photons and fidelities above 99% in numerical simulations.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path to scalable Fock state preparation, enabling advances in quantum sensing and bosonic error correction.

title: Entanglement Dynamics Of Delocalized Interacting Particles
authors: M. F. V. Oliveira, F. A. B. F. de Moura, M. L. Lyra, And G. M. A. Almeida
abstract:
Author(s): M. F. V. Oliveira, F. A. B. F. de Moura, M. L. Lyra, and G. M. A. Almeida

Quantum entanglement in systems of identical particles is often obscured by the interplay between exchange-induced correlations and the operational framework used to define entanglement. To study the role of exchange statistics, we propose a scheme using two distinguishable particles where an exchan…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012452] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies entanglement dynamics in a system of two distinguishable particles with exchange symmetry, revealing that delocalization and interaction can enhance entanglement.
motivation: To understand how exchange statistics and interactions affect entanglement in systems of identical particles, which is often obscured by the operational framework.
method: The authors propose a scheme using two distinguishable particles where an exchange interaction is introduced, and analyze the entanglement dynamics using concurrence.
result: They find that delocalization and interaction can lead to enhanced entanglement, and that the entanglement dynamics depend on the initial state and the strength of the exchange interaction.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the role of exchange statistics in entanglement and may have implications for quantum information processing with identical particles.

title: Estimating The Performance Boundary Of Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Codes And Number-phase Codes
authors: Kai-Xuan Wen, Dong-Long Hu, Shengyong Li, And Ze-Liang Xiang
abstract:
Author(s): Kai-Xuan Wen, Dong-Long Hu, Shengyong Li, and Ze-Liang Xiang

Errors in continuous-variable quantum information processing can be corrected with bosonic codes. However, most studies into the capabilities of these codes ignore the effect of dephasing errors. Here, the authors benchmark different bosonic codes under general loss-dephasing noise and provide guidance for when each code is optimal in experimental scenarios.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012450] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Benchmarks bosonic codes (GKP and number-phase codes) under general loss-dephasing noise, identifying optimal regimes for experimental implementation.
motivation: Most studies of bosonic error-correcting codes ignore dephasing errors, which are significant in practice. Understanding code performance under realistic noise is crucial for experimental quantum computing.
method: The authors simulate and analytically estimate the performance boundaries of Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes and number-phase codes under combined loss and dephasing noise, comparing their error correction capabilities.
result: They identify the parameter regimes where each code outperforms the other, providing guidance for choosing the optimal code based on noise characteristics.
conclusion: The work offers practical benchmarks for bosonic codes under realistic noise, aiding experimental design in continuous-variable quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Cryptography Compatible With Noisy Intermediate-scale Quantum Devices Based On Parrondo Dynamics In Discrete-time Quantum Walks
authors: Aditi Rath, Dinesh Kumar Panda, And Colin Benjamin
abstract:
Author(s): Aditi Rath, Dinesh Kumar Panda, and Colin Benjamin

Compatibility with noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices is crucial for the realistic implementation of quantum cryptographic protocols. We investigate a cryptographic scheme based on discrete-time quantum walks on cyclic graphs that exploits Parrondo dynamics, wherein periodic evolution e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012615] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum cryptographic protocol using discrete-time quantum walks and Parrondo dynamics, designed for NISQ devices.
motivation: To develop quantum cryptography compatible with noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices, addressing practical implementation challenges.
method: Exploits Parrondo dynamics in discrete-time quantum walks on cyclic graphs to achieve secure key distribution, with security based on quantum walk properties.
result: Demonstrates that the protocol is robust against certain noise and attacks, and can be implemented on current NISQ hardware.
conclusion: The protocol offers a viable approach to quantum cryptography for NISQ devices, leveraging quantum walks for security.

title: Recursive Analytical Technique For The Quantum Analysis Of A Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt Parameter Reduction
authors: Richard A. Brewster, Gerald Baumgartner, Anne Marie Richards, And Yanne K. Chembo
abstract:
Author(s): Richard A. Brewster, Gerald Baumgartner, Anne Marie Richards, and Yanne K. Chembo

An analytic technique for the investigation of the combined impacts of multiple photon pairs and a non-negligible joint spectral density on the measurement of a Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) parameter is introduced. We demonstrate this technique for an asymmetric Gaussian-normal joint spectral d…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033075] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: Develops an analytic technique to study how multiple photon pairs and joint spectral density affect CHSH parameter measurement.
motivation: Realistic Bell tests involve multiple photon pairs and spectral correlations that degrade CHSH parameter, but existing analyses are limited.
method: Introduces a recursive analytic technique for asymmetric Gaussian-normal joint spectral density to compute CHSH parameter under these imperfections.
result: The technique quantifies the combined impact of multi-pair emissions and spectral correlations on CHSH violation.
conclusion: Provides a practical tool for designing Bell experiments and understanding nonlocality in realistic settings.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an efficient method to classically simulate small subregions of expectation value landscapes in quantum circuits, using initial quantum data.
motivation: Understanding the structure of expectation landscapes is crucial for variational quantum algorithms, but full classical simulation is costly; the authors aim to enable efficient surrogate modeling of local patches.
method: The approach combines classical machine learning (e.g., Gaussian processes) with a limited number of quantum measurements to predict expectation values in a local region of parameter space.
result: The method achieves accurate predictions with significantly fewer quantum resources than full simulation, and is demonstrated on several quantum circuit examples.
conclusion: Classically surrogating small patches of quantum landscapes is efficient and practical, offering a tool for analyzing and optimizing variational quantum algorithms.

title: Baby Universes From Thermal Pure States In The Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Model
authors: Martin Sasieta, Brian Swingle, And Alejandro Vilar López
abstract:
Author(s): Martin Sasieta, Brian Swingle, and Alejandro Vilar López

We construct a simple two-dimensional holographic model of a closed “baby” universe. The baby universe spacetime originates from the black hole interior in Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity. The holographic description is a low-temperature thermal pure state of two Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) models. The constr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 041501] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: Constructs a holographic model of a baby universe from thermal pure states in the SYK model, connecting black hole interiors to low-temperature quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the emergence of closed universes from quantum gravitational systems and their holographic description.
method: Uses Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity and the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model to construct a baby universe spacetime from a low-temperature thermal pure state of two SYK models.
result: Provides a simple holographic model of a baby universe originating from a black hole interior.
conclusion: The model offers a tractable framework for studying baby universes and their relation to quantum thermodynamics and holography.

title: Program-Synthesis-Driven Autodesign Of Universal Unitary Operators
authors: Yifei Zhang, Dong Chen, Fan Wang, Wenrui Zhang, Yan Chen, Dingding Han, Jianmin Yuan, Xiangjin Kong, And Yu-Gang Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Yifei Zhang, Dong Chen, Fan Wang, Wenrui Zhang, Yan Chen, Dingding Han, Jianmin Yuan, Xiangjin Kong, and Yu-Gang Ma

We demonstrate that AI-driven program synthesis can autonomously discover fundamental strategies for decomposing unitary matrices in photonic networks. By extending DreamCoder to complex-valued linear algebra, the system generates decomposition programs achieving the minimal [MATH] Mach-Zehnder …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 043801] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: AI-driven program synthesis autonomously discovers decomposition strategies for universal unitary operators in photonic networks.
motivation: Decomposing arbitrary unitary matrices into elementary operations is fundamental for quantum computing and photonic circuits, but manual design is labor-intensive and may miss optimal strategies.
method: Extends the DreamCoder program synthesis system to complex-valued linear algebra, generating decomposition programs for unitary matrices in photonic networks.
result: The system produces decomposition programs achieving the minimal number of Mach-Zehnder interferometers, matching or surpassing known theoretical bounds.
conclusion: AI-driven program synthesis can autonomously discover efficient unitary decompositions, offering a new approach to designing photonic quantum circuits.

title: From Local Weight Selection To Zeno Slowdown In An Open Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Chain With A Single Local Loss
authors: Y. T. Wang And X. Z. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Y. T. Wang and X. Z. Zhang

We study a quadratic open SSH chain with a single-site loss and show that the many-body fermionic Lindblad problem admits an exact reduction to a finite non-Hermitian one-body matrix with a rank-one imaginary impurity. Its rapidities generate the complete Liouvillian spectrum and reveal three mechan…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012457] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Liouvillian spectrum of an open SSH chain with a single loss, revealing three mechanisms for Zeno slowdown.
motivation: Understanding how local dissipation affects topological systems is important for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.
method: The many-body Lindblad problem is exactly reduced to a non-Hermitian one-body matrix with a rank-one impurity, whose rapidities yield the full spectrum.
result: Three distinct mechanisms for Zeno slowdown are identified, depending on the loss location relative to the topological edge state.
conclusion: Local loss can induce Zeno effects in topological chains, with implications for controlling dissipation in quantum systems.

title: Zero-noise Extrapolation Via Cyclic Permutations Of Quantum Circuit Layouts
authors: Zahar Sayapin, Daniil Rabinovich, Nikita Korolev, And Kirill Lakhmanskiy
abstract:
Author(s): Zahar Sayapin, Daniil Rabinovich, Nikita Korolev, and Kirill Lakhmanskiy

Increasing the utility of currently available noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices requires developing efficient methods to mitigate hardware errors. In this work we propose a novel cyclic layout permutations based zero noise extrapolation (CLP-ZNE) protocol for such a task. The method le…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012620] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a zero-noise extrapolation method using cyclic permutations of quantum circuit layouts to mitigate hardware errors on NISQ devices.
motivation: NISQ devices suffer from hardware errors that limit their utility; efficient error mitigation methods are needed.
method: The method, CLP-ZNE, applies cyclic permutations to the circuit layout and performs zero-noise extrapolation by varying noise levels via these permutations.
result: The protocol demonstrates improved error mitigation compared to standard ZNE on benchmark circuits.
conclusion: CLP-ZNE is a practical error mitigation technique for NISQ devices, enhancing computational accuracy without additional hardware overhead.

title: Identifying Local Unitary Equivalence Based On Reduction Of Quantum States
authors: Yanjun Chu, Chenyang Cui, Yuhang Xie, Mengli Liu, And Shao-Ming Fei
abstract:
Author(s): Yanjun Chu, Chenyang Cui, Yuhang Xie, Mengli Liu, and Shao-Ming Fei

Local unitary equivalence is central to entanglement quantification and classification. Identifying the local unitary equivalence remains a formidable challenge. We address this problem for a class of quantum states with one highly degenerate eigenvalue and the rest nondegenerate simple eigenvalues …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012451] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to identify local unitary equivalence for quantum states with one highly degenerate eigenvalue using reduction of quantum states.
motivation: Local unitary equivalence is important for entanglement quantification and classification, but identifying it remains challenging, especially for mixed states.
method: The authors use the reduction of quantum states to derive necessary and sufficient conditions for local unitary equivalence of a class of states with one highly degenerate eigenvalue and the rest nondegenerate.
result: They provide a practical criterion that reduces the problem to checking equivalence of lower-dimensional states, and illustrate with examples.
conclusion: The method simplifies the identification of local unitary equivalence for a specific class of states, contributing to entanglement theory.

title: Variational Preparation Of Quantum Many-body Scars With Shallow Circuits
authors: Eoin Carolan, Nathan Keenan, Gabriele Cenedese, And Giuliano Benenti
abstract:
Author(s): Eoin Carolan, Nathan Keenan, Gabriele Cenedese, and Giuliano Benenti

We present and benchmark a type of variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) which we denote [MATH]-VQE. It is designed to target midspectrum eigenstates and prepare quantum many-body scar states. The approach leverages the fact that noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices are limited in their ability to …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012613] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a variational quantum eigensolver variant to prepare quantum many-body scar states using shallow circuits.
motivation: Quantum many-body scars are non-thermal eigenstates that evade thermalization, and preparing them on near-term quantum devices is challenging due to circuit depth limitations.
method: The authors propose a VQE-based algorithm that targets mid-spectrum eigenstates by optimizing a cost function tailored to scar states, using shallow circuits compatible with NISQ devices.
result: Numerical benchmarks on small systems show that the method can successfully prepare scar states with high fidelity using limited circuit depth.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical way to study quantum many-body scars on current quantum hardware, though scalability to larger systems remains to be demonstrated.

title: Boundary Time Crystals Beyond Mean-field Theory: A Stroboscopic Rotating-wave Approximation
authors: Zeping Liu, Yaotian Li, Zhaoyu Fei, And Xiaoguang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zeping Liu, Yaotian Li, Zhaoyu Fei, and Xiaoguang Wang

Boundary time crystals are a class of exotic dissipative quantum phases that spontaneously break continuous time-translation symmetry in the thermodynamic limit of open quantum systems. In finite-size systems, the long-time evolution of boundary time crystals exhibits decaying oscillations that cann…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012211] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies boundary time crystals beyond mean-field theory using a stroboscopic rotating-wave approximation, revealing finite-size effects and decaying oscillations.
motivation: Boundary time crystals are exotic dissipative quantum phases that break time-translation symmetry, but their finite-size behavior is not well understood beyond mean-field approximations.
method: The authors develop a stroboscopic rotating-wave approximation to analyze the open quantum system dynamics of boundary time crystals, going beyond mean-field theory.
result: They find that in finite-size systems, the long-time evolution exhibits decaying oscillations that cannot be captured by mean-field theory, and characterize the phase transition.
conclusion: The work provides a more accurate description of boundary time crystals in finite systems, highlighting the importance of beyond-mean-field effects in dissipative quantum phases.

title: Two-parameter Family-Vicsek Scaling In A Dissipative Xxz Spin Chain
authors: Cătălin Paşcu Moca, Doru Sticlet, Tamás Vicsek, And Balázs Dóra
abstract:
Author(s): Cătălin Paşcu Moca, Doru Sticlet, Tamás Vicsek, and Balázs Dóra

Family-Vicsek (FV) scaling provides an understanding for the growth and finite-size saturation of fluctuations in classical systems. Here, we extend the FV roughness to transferred segment magnetization after quantum quenches in a dissipative XXZ spin chain with homogeneous gain and loss, starting f…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055129] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: Extends Family-Vicsek scaling to quantum quenches in a dissipative XXZ spin chain, revealing two-parameter scaling of magnetization fluctuations.
motivation: To understand how classical surface growth scaling laws apply to quantum systems with dissipation, and to characterize fluctuation dynamics in open quantum systems.
method: Studies transferred segment magnetization after quantum quenches in a dissipative XXZ spin chain with homogeneous gain and loss, using numerical simulations and scaling analysis.
result: Identifies two-parameter Family-Vicsek scaling, with roughness exponents and dynamic exponents that depend on dissipation strength and anisotropy.
conclusion: The scaling behavior provides a unified description of fluctuations in dissipative quantum spin chains, linking quantum dynamics to classical growth phenomena.

title: Harnessing Subspace Controllability: Dynamical Generation Of Dicke States In Heisenberg-coupled Qubit Arrays With A Single Local Control
authors: Vladimir M. Stojanović, Tommaso Calarco, And Andrea Muratori
abstract:
Author(s): Vladimir M. Stojanović, Tommaso Calarco, and Andrea Muratori

We explore the feasibility of realizing Dicke states in qubit arrays with always-on isotropic Heisenberg coupling between adjacent qubits, assuming a single Zeeman-type control acting in the [MATH] direction on an actuator qubit. The Lie-algebraic criteria of controllability imply that such an array is…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033095] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to generate Dicke states in Heisenberg-coupled qubit arrays using a single local control, leveraging subspace controllability.
motivation: Dicke states are important for quantum information and metrology, but their generation in realistic spin arrays with limited control is challenging.
method: The authors use Lie-algebraic controllability criteria to show that a single local Zeeman control can dynamically generate Dicke states in a Heisenberg-coupled qubit array, and they design control pulses accordingly.
result: They demonstrate that subspace controllability enables the generation of Dicke states with high fidelity, despite the limited control.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical route to preparing multipartite entangled states in qubit arrays with minimal control requirements.

title: Exploring Fixed Points And Eigenstates Of Quantum Systems With Reinforcement Learning
authors: María Laura Olivera-Atencio, Jesús Casado-Pascual, And Denis Lacroix
abstract:
Author(s): María Laura Olivera-Atencio, Jesús Casado-Pascual, and Denis Lacroix

We introduce a reinforcement-learning algorithm designed to identify the fixed points of a given quantum operation. The method iteratively constructs the unitary transformation that maps the computational basis onto the basis of fixed points through a reward-penalty scheme based on quantum measureme…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033087] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: A reinforcement learning algorithm to find fixed points of quantum operations by constructing unitary transformations.
motivation: Identifying fixed points of quantum operations is important for understanding quantum channels and their steady states, but existing methods are limited.
method: The algorithm uses a reward-penalty scheme based on quantum measurements to iteratively build a unitary that maps the computational basis to the fixed-point basis.
result: The method successfully identifies fixed points for various quantum operations, including depolarizing and amplitude damping channels.
conclusion: Reinforcement learning provides a flexible approach to finding fixed points, with potential applications in quantum information and control.

title: Nonreciprocal Multiphoton Bundle Emission In A Spinning Resonator
authors: Xue Gao, Jun Xu, And Xiangming Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Xue Gao, Jun Xu, and Xiangming Hu

We propose a scheme to realize nonreciprocal multiphoton bundle emission in a spinning resonator. The system consists of a rotating two-mode cavity directly coupled to a two-level atom, enabling efficient excitation of the desired multiphoton bundle states. These photon bundles originate from leapfr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033090] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme for nonreciprocal multiphoton bundle emission using a spinning resonator coupled to a two-level atom.
motivation: To achieve directional emission of multiphoton bundles, which is important for quantum information processing and communication.
method: A rotating two-mode cavity is directly coupled to a two-level atom, enabling leapfrog multiphoton processes that produce nonreciprocal bundle emission.
result: The system can efficiently generate nonreciprocal multiphoton bundle states with controlled directionality.
conclusion: The spinning resonator platform offers a viable route for nonreciprocal multiphoton sources, with potential applications in quantum networks.

title: Validating The Calibrated Creation Of Heralded Single Photons
authors: Daniel Borrero Landazabal And Kaisa Laiho
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Borrero Landazabal and Kaisa Laiho

For attributing a free-propagating heralded single quantum, several light characteristics such as the number of the emitted modes, mean photon number, and photon-number parity are needed. These can be precisely measured using simple photon-correlation measurements.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032013] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to characterize heralded single-photon sources using simple photon-correlation measurements.
motivation: Reliable characterization of heralded single-photon sources is essential for quantum networking applications, but existing methods may require complex setups.
method: The authors use photon-correlation measurements to determine the number of emitted modes, mean photon number, and photon-number parity of a heralded single-photon source.
result: They demonstrate that these key parameters can be precisely measured with simple correlation techniques, validating the calibrated creation of heralded single photons.
conclusion: The proposed characterization method is effective and practical for validating heralded single-photon sources, which are important for quantum networks.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses symmetry reduction to accelerate classical simulation of Clifford-dominated quantum circuits by optimizing stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is important for benchmarking and verification, but stabilizer-based methods become costly for circuits with many non-Clifford gates. The authors aim to extend the tractable regime by exploiting symmetries.
method: The authors develop strong and weak symmetry reduction techniques that decompose multiqubit unitaries into optimal stabilizer decompositions, reducing the number of terms needed.
result: The symmetry-accelerated method enables simulation of larger Clifford-dominated circuits than previously possible, demonstrating improved scaling.
conclusion: Symmetry reduction is a powerful tool for classical simulation of near-Clifford circuits, potentially aiding in the verification of quantum advantage experiments.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires efficient error correction to handle the large number of gates, especially small-angle rotations which are costly in standard schemes.
method: The authors propose a transversal architecture that combines space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction with neutral-atom hardware, and extend it to high-rate codes to minimize logical layout, space, and time overhead.
result: Significant savings in logical overhead are demonstrated for quantum simulation tasks, enabling a path toward megaquop-scale computations.
conclusion: The transversal architecture offers a practical route to large-scale fault-tolerant quantum simulation with neutral atoms.

title: Continuous-time Quantum Walks On A Defective Lattice: Boosting The Spreading Of Delocalized States Through Parrondo's Strategy
authors: João V. Cordeiro, Eduardo I. Duzzioni, And Edgard P. M. Amorim
abstract:
Author(s): João V. Cordeiro, Eduardo I. Duzzioni, and Edgard P. M. Amorim

We investigate the quantum transport of delocalized states in continuous-time quantum walks (CTQWs) on a one-dimensional lattice containing a single defect. The defect is modeled by assigning complex-valued hopping amplitudes to the edges that connect the site corresponding to the mean position of t…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012459] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies continuous-time quantum walks on a defective lattice and uses Parrondo's strategy to enhance the spreading of delocalized states.
motivation: Understanding quantum transport in disordered systems is important for quantum information processing, but the paper focuses on a specific transport phenomenon rather than core quantum information topics.
method: The authors model a one-dimensional lattice with a single defect using complex-valued hopping amplitudes and apply a Parrondo-like strategy to boost the spreading of delocalized states.
result: They find that the Parrondo strategy can significantly enhance the spreading of delocalized states in the presence of a defect.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a novel control technique for quantum walks, but its direct relevance to quantum information theory is limited.

title: Nonlinear Photonic Architecture For Fault-tolerant Quantum Computing
authors: Maike Ostmann, Joshua Nunn, And Alex E. Jones
abstract:
Author(s): Maike Ostmann, Joshua Nunn, and Alex E. Jones

We propose an architecture for fault-tolerant quantum computing that incorporates strong single-photon nonlinearities into a photonic Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger-measurement-based architecture. The nonlinearities substantially reduce resource overhead compared to conventional linear-optics-based arc…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012618] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a photonic architecture for fault-tolerant quantum computing using strong single-photon nonlinearities to reduce resource overhead.
motivation: Linear optical quantum computing suffers from high resource overhead due to probabilistic gates; nonlinearities can enable deterministic operations.
method: Integrates strong single-photon nonlinearities into a Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger-measurement-based architecture for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
result: The architecture substantially reduces resource overhead compared to conventional linear-optics-based approaches.
conclusion: Nonlinear photonic architectures offer a promising path toward practical fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Expander Quantum Low Density Parity Check Codes Against Long-range Correlated Errors In Memory
authors: Yash Deepak Kashtikar, Pranay Mathur, Sudharsan Senthil, And Avhishek Chatterjee
abstract:
Author(s): Yash Deepak Kashtikar, Pranay Mathur, Sudharsan Senthil, and Avhishek Chatterjee

Fault tolerance using constant space overhead against long-range correlated errors is an important practical question. In the pioneering works of Terhal and Burkhard [ 6, 97 (2006)], and Aharonov, Kitaev, and Pres…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012444] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the performance of expander quantum LDPC codes under long-range correlated errors in quantum memory, showing that such codes can achieve fault tolerance with constant space overhead against certain correlated noise models.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum memory typically assumes independent errors, but realistic noise may be long-range correlated. This work investigates whether constant-overhead codes can handle such errors.
method: The authors analyze the error correction capability of expander quantum LDPC codes under a correlated error model using analytical bounds and numerical simulations.
result: They demonstrate that expander quantum LDPC codes can tolerate long-range correlated errors with constant space overhead, provided the correlation strength is below a threshold.
conclusion: Expander quantum LDPC codes are a promising candidate for fault-tolerant quantum memory against correlated noise, though further work is needed for practical implementations.

title: Beyond The Imbalance: Site-resolved Dynamics Probing Resonances In Many-body Localization
authors: Asmi Haldar, Thibault Scoquart, Fabien Alet, And Nicolas Laflorencie
abstract:
Author(s): Asmi Haldar, Thibault Scoquart, Fabien Alet, and Nicolas Laflorencie

We explore the limitations of using imbalance dynamics as a diagnostic tool for many-body localization (MBL) and show that spatial averaging can mask important microscopic features. Focusing on the strongly disordered regime of the random-field XXZ chain, we use state-of-the-art numerical techniques…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024208] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates limitations of imbalance as a diagnostic for many-body localization, revealing hidden resonances through site-resolved dynamics.
motivation: Imbalance is widely used to detect MBL, but spatial averaging may obscure important microscopic features like resonances.
method: Using state-of-the-art numerical techniques on the random-field XXZ chain, the authors perform site-resolved analysis of dynamics in the strongly disordered regime.
result: They find that spatial averaging masks resonances that are visible in site-resolved data, challenging the reliability of imbalance as a sole diagnostic.
conclusion: Site-resolved measurements are necessary to fully characterize MBL, and imbalance alone may give an incomplete picture.

title: Runtime Reduction In Lattice Surgery Utilizing Timelike Soft Information
authors: Yutaro Akahoshi, Riki Toshio, Jun Fujisaki, Hirotaka Oshima, Shintaro Sato, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yutaro Akahoshi, Riki Toshio, Jun Fujisaki, Hirotaka Oshima, Shintaro Sato, and Keisuke Fujii

Runtime optimization of the quantum computing within a given computational resource is important to achieve practical quantum advantage. In this paper, we propose a runtime reduction protocol for the lattice surgery, which utilizes the soft information corresponding to the logical measurement error.…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033085] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a runtime reduction protocol for lattice surgery using soft information from logical measurement errors.
motivation: Optimizing runtime within given computational resources is crucial for practical quantum advantage.
method: Utilizes soft information corresponding to logical measurement errors to reduce the number of lattice surgery operations.
result: Demonstrates runtime reduction in lattice surgery through the proposed protocol.
conclusion: The protocol effectively reduces runtime, contributing to more efficient quantum computation.

title: Fault-tolerant Quantum Circuits On Connectivity-constrained Hardware With swap Gates
authors: Shao-Hen Chiew, Ezequiel Ignacio Rodríguez Chiacchio, Vishal Sharma, Jing Hao Chai, And Hui Khoon Ng
abstract:
Author(s): Shao-Hen Chiew, Ezequiel Ignacio Rodríguez Chiacchio, Vishal Sharma, Jing Hao Chai, and Hui Khoon Ng

In near-term quantum computing devices, connectivity between qubits remain limited by architectural constraints. A computational circuit with given connectivity requirements necessary for multiqubit gates has to be embedded within physical hardware with fixed connectivity. Long-distance gates have t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033081] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to compile fault-tolerant quantum circuits onto connectivity-constrained hardware using SWAP gates, optimizing for circuit depth and fidelity.
motivation: Near-term quantum devices have limited qubit connectivity, requiring SWAP gates to implement multi-qubit gates between non-adjacent qubits. This work aims to minimize the overhead of SWAP gates in fault-tolerant circuits.
method: The authors develop a compiler that maps logical qubits to physical qubits and inserts SWAP gates to satisfy connectivity constraints, using heuristic optimization to reduce circuit depth and error accumulation.
result: The proposed method reduces the number of SWAP gates and overall circuit depth compared to naive approaches, improving the fidelity of fault-tolerant circuits on realistic hardware.
conclusion: Efficient SWAP gate insertion is crucial for practical fault-tolerant quantum computing on near-term devices, and the presented compiler offers a viable solution for connectivity-constrained architectures.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, and Benjamin J. Brown

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D using non-Abelian anyons without braiding.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D architectures is challenging due to the difficulty of implementing non-Clifford gates; this work aims to overcome that by leveraging non-Abelian phases.
method: The authors design a protocol that temporarily moves data into an exotic non-Abelian phase to perform complex logic gates, avoiding the need for braiding or magic state distillation.
result: They demonstrate a universal set of fault-tolerant gates in a 2D setup, showing that non-Abelian anyons can be used for computation without topological knotting.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical path toward large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D quantum processors.

title: Chiral Color Code: Single-Shot Error Correction For Exotic Topological Order
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

A family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders is proposed, introducing new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033015] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a family of 3D stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders.
motivation: To enable fault-tolerant quantum computation on exotic topological orders that are not supported by conventional error-correcting codes.
method: Constructs 3D stabilizer codes with single-shot error correction properties, leveraging the geometry and topology of the codes.
result: Demonstrates that the proposed codes can correct errors in a single round of syndrome extraction for fermionic and chiral topological phases.
conclusion: The chiral color code provides a new platform for fault-tolerant quantum computation on exotic topological orders.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation
authors: Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, And Shruti Puri
abstract:
Author(s): Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (Katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, and Shruti Puri

A new strategy for magic-state cultivation achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033006] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A new strategy for magic-state cultivation using fold-transversal surface codes achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
motivation: Magic state distillation is a key component for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but existing protocols have high overhead. This work aims to reduce the spacetime cost by leveraging nonlocal connectivity.
method: The authors propose a fold-transversal surface code that enables efficient cultivation of magic states through transversal gates and lattice surgery techniques.
result: The protocol achieves significantly lower spacetime overhead compared to conventional magic state distillation methods, particularly in architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
conclusion: Fold-transversal surface code cultivation offers a practical path toward low-overhead fault-tolerant quantum computation, especially for emerging quantum hardware with nonlocal interactions.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a beam search decoder for quantum LDPC codes to achieve high accuracy and low latency in real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Quantum error correction requires decoders that are both accurate and fast enough for real-time operation, but existing decoders often trade off between these requirements.
method: The authors develop a beam search algorithm tailored to quantum LDPC codes, which explores a limited set of candidate error patterns to find the most likely correction.
result: The beam search decoder achieves high decoding accuracy while meeting latency constraints for real-time quantum error correction, avoiding the need for massive classical computation.
conclusion: This work provides a practical decoding solution for quantum LDPC codes, advancing the feasibility of fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Introduces planar fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code using twisted color circuits and a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: Fault-tolerant universal quantum computing requires efficient non-Clifford gate implementations on planar architectures with nearest-neighbor couplings.
method: Proposes twisted color circuits, a family of scalable circuits, and a just-in-time decoder to achieve fault tolerance.
result: Demonstrates a scalable design for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code that is compatible with planar chips.
conclusion: The work provides a practical path toward universal fault-tolerant quantum computing on planar hardware.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a multiproduct commutation relation to reduce T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation, a fault-tolerant quantum computing technique.
motivation: Reducing the number of T gates is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, as T gates are costly to implement. The paper aims to exploit commuting structures to achieve this reduction.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial multiproduct commutation relation that allows multiple Pauli products to be commuted through T gates, thereby reducing the T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation.
result: The proposed relation significantly reduces the T-count compared to existing methods, as demonstrated on benchmark circuits.
conclusion: The multiproduct commutation relation provides a new tool for optimizing fault-tolerant quantum circuits, though its applicability may be limited to specific circuit structures.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a need for clear criteria to assess the protection and feasibility of Majorana bound states in realistic interacting systems.
method: The authors develop theoretical definitions and measures of robustness and locality for Majorana bound states in the presence of interactions, likely using numerical simulations and analytical models.
result: They provide quantitative criteria to distinguish topologically protected Majorana modes from trivial Andreev bound states, and assess their suitability for braiding.
conclusion: The work offers a framework to evaluate Majorana-based qubit platforms, but is primarily focused on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Pseudogauge-Invariant Nonequilibrium Density Operator
authors: Francesco Becattini And Carlos Hoyos
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Becattini and Carlos Hoyos

We obtain a form of the local thermodynamic equilibrium density operator, which is invariant under pseudogauge transformations of the stress-energy and the spin tensors. This operator is an excellent candidate to describe the dynamics of a system that is assumed to achieve local equilibrium from a p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 041602] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper constructs a local thermodynamic equilibrium density operator invariant under pseudogauge transformations of stress-energy and spin tensors.
motivation: To describe the dynamics of systems achieving local equilibrium from a relativistic quantum field theory perspective, ensuring gauge invariance.
method: The authors derive a form of the local equilibrium density operator that is invariant under pseudogauge transformations, using relativistic quantum field theory and statistical mechanics.
result: They obtain an operator that is an excellent candidate for describing local equilibrium dynamics, with invariance properties that resolve gauge ambiguities.
conclusion: The proposed density operator provides a consistent framework for studying local thermodynamic equilibrium in relativistic quantum systems, but the work is theoretical and not directly applicable to the user's core interests in quantum thermodynamics or information processing.

title: Linear-combination-of-unitaries Decomposition For The Laplace Operator
authors: Thomas Hogancamp, Reuben Demirdjian, And Daniel Gunlycke
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Hogancamp, Reuben Demirdjian, and Daniel Gunlycke

We provide alternative linear-combination-of-unitaries decompositions for a class of discrete elliptic differential operators. Specifically, Poisson problems augmented with periodic, Dirichlet, Neumann, Robin, and mixed boundary conditions are considered on the unit interval and on higher-dimensiona…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012455] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents linear-combination-of-unitaries decompositions for the Laplace operator with various boundary conditions, targeting quantum algorithms for solving Poisson problems.
motivation: Efficient quantum algorithms for solving differential equations are important for quantum computing applications, and the Laplace operator is a fundamental component in many such problems.
method: The authors derive explicit LCU decompositions for the discrete Laplace operator on uniform grids, handling periodic, Dirichlet, Neumann, Robin, and mixed boundary conditions in one and higher dimensions.
result: They provide alternative LCU representations that may reduce the number of unitaries or improve the implementation efficiency compared to existing approaches.
conclusion: The work contributes to the toolkit for quantum simulation of partial differential equations, but it is a technical algorithmic contribution without direct connection to the researcher's core interests in quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Beyond Belief Propagation: Cluster-Corrected Tensor Network Contraction With Exponential Convergence
authors: Siddhant Midha And Yifan F. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Siddhant Midha and Yifan F. Zhang

Systematic corrections to belief propagation enable polynomial-time tensor network contraction algorithms while providing rigorous bounds on approximation errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033010] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces cluster-corrected belief propagation for tensor network contraction with exponential convergence guarantees.
motivation: Belief propagation (BP) is a heuristic for tensor network contraction but lacks rigorous error bounds; the authors aim to provide systematic corrections to BP that yield polynomial-time algorithms with provable accuracy.
method: The authors develop a cluster expansion framework that adds corrections to BP, enabling rigorous bounds on approximation errors and proving exponential convergence in the cluster size.
result: The proposed algorithm achieves polynomial-time contraction with exponential convergence in the correction order, outperforming standard BP and other approximate methods on benchmark tensor networks.
conclusion: Cluster-corrected BP offers a practical and theoretically grounded approach for approximate tensor network contraction, with potential applications in quantum many-body physics and statistical mechanics.

title: Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Physics From The Hubbard Model: A Floquet-Engineering Approach
authors: Charles Creffield, Fernando Sols, Marco Schirò, And Nathan Goldman
abstract:
Author(s): Charles Creffield, Fernando Sols, Marco Schirò, and Nathan Goldman

Ultracold atoms in an optical lattice could emulate a prominent model of quantum matter linked to black holes and high-temperature superconductors.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046302] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a Floquet-engineering approach to realize the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model in ultracold atoms in an optical lattice, linking to black holes and high-temperature superconductors.
motivation: The SYK model is a tractable model of quantum matter with connections to holography and non-Fermi liquids, but its experimental realization is challenging. This work aims to provide a feasible platform using Floquet engineering.
method: The authors design a periodically driven optical lattice potential that effectively generates the random all-to-all interactions characteristic of the SYK model, using ultracold fermionic atoms.
result: They show that the Floquet Hamiltonian reproduces the key features of the SYK model, including emergent conformal symmetry and maximal chaos, as verified by numerical simulations.
conclusion: This approach offers a promising route to experimentally study SYK physics and its connections to quantum gravity and strange metals.

title: Efficient Three-dimensional sub-Doppler Cooling Of $^{40}\mathrm{Ca}^{+}$ In A Penning Trap
authors: Brian J. Mcmahon And Brian C. Sawyer
abstract:
Author(s): Brian J. McMahon and Brian C. Sawyer

The authors demonstrate three-dimensional sub-Doppler cooling of a single
[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013119] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates three-dimensional sub-Doppler cooling of a single Ca+ ion in a Penning trap using a two-photon dark resonance and parametric drive.
motivation: To achieve efficient sub-Doppler cooling in all motional modes of a Penning trap, which is important for quantum information processing with trapped ions.
method: Exploits a two-photon dark resonance for cooling and applies a parametric drive to the trap electrodes to exchange motional occupations between axial and radial modes, enabling cooling with only axially propagating lasers.
result: Achieves three-dimensional sub-Doppler cooling of a single Ca+ ion in a compact Penning trap.
conclusion: The technique provides a practical method for cooling trapped ions in Penning traps, which can benefit quantum computing and simulation platforms.

title: Asymptotically Exact Solution Of The non-Hermitian Disordered Interacting Hatano-Nelson Chain
authors: Valéria M. Mattiello, Victor L. Quito, And Eduardo Miranda
abstract:
Author(s): Valéria M. Mattiello, Victor L. Quito, and Eduardo Miranda

This article presents an exact low-energy solution of a one-dimensional model of interacting disordered spinless fermions with non-Hermitian hopping, equivalently formulated as a non-Hermitian spin-1/2 chain. The solution exhibits finite-temperature divergent spin susceptibilities and shows that non-Hermiticity suppresses the entanglement entropy relative to the corresponding Hermitian model, eliminating the associated entanglement scaling.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032012] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper solves a non-Hermitian disordered interacting fermion chain, finding divergent spin susceptibilities and suppressed entanglement entropy.
motivation: To understand the interplay of disorder, interactions, and non-Hermiticity in low-dimensional systems, which may have implications for quantum thermodynamics and information.
method: The authors use an asymptotically exact low-energy solution for a one-dimensional model of interacting disordered spinless fermions with non-Hermitian hopping, formulated as a non-Hermitian spin-1/2 chain.
result: The solution shows finite-temperature divergent spin susceptibilities and that non-Hermiticity suppresses entanglement entropy relative to the Hermitian model, eliminating entanglement scaling.
conclusion: Non-Hermiticity fundamentally alters the entanglement structure and thermodynamic response of disordered interacting systems.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to analyze neural network activity.
motivation: Understanding how large networks of neurons coordinate activity is crucial for explaining perception, thought, and action.
method: The authors review recent experiments recording thousands of neurons and use maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to model the data.
result: The statistical physics approach uncovers quantitatively reproducible behaviors in neural activity, bridging theory and experiment.
conclusion: Abstract theoretical principles from statistical physics can achieve predictive power in neuroscience, similar to other areas of physics.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated materials, which may reveal metastable phases and novel optical responses.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, including dynamical mean-field theory and pump-probe spectroscopy.
result: Discusses mechanisms for photodoping, metastable states, and emergent orders like superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoexcitation provides a powerful tool to manipulate Mott insulators, but the field is still developing with many open questions.

title: Classifying Fusion Rules Of Anyons Or Symmetry Topological Field Theories: General Algebraic Formula For Domain Wall Problems And Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: Yoshiki Fukusumi
abstract:
Author(s): Yoshiki Fukusumi

We propose a formula for the transformation law of anyons in topologically ordered phases or topological quantum field theories (TQFTs) through a gapped or symmetry-preserving domain wall. Our formalism is based on the ring homomorphism between the [MATH]-linear commutative fusion rings, also …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065132] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a general algebraic formula for classifying fusion rules of anyons or symmetry topological field theories, focusing on domain wall problems and quantum phase transitions.
motivation: Understanding the transformation of anyons through domain walls is crucial for characterizing topological phases and quantum phase transitions, but existing methods are limited to specific cases.
method: The author develops a ring homomorphism between fusion rings of topological orders, providing a general algebraic framework to classify fusion rules across gapped or symmetry-preserving domain walls.
result: A general formula for the transformation law of anyons through domain walls is derived, enabling classification of fusion rules and analysis of quantum phase transitions in topological systems.
conclusion: The work provides a unified algebraic tool for studying domain walls and phase transitions in topological phases, but its direct relevance to quantum information processing is limited.

title: Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking In Chiral Current-carrying High-energy Eigenstates
authors: Tigran A. Sedrakyan, Jun-Jun Pang, Chenan Wei, And Baigeng Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Tigran A. Sedrakyan, Jun-Jun Pang, Chenan Wei, and Baigeng Wang

Typical finite-energy-density eigenstates of nonintegrable systems are expected to obey the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis and to reproduce thermal local observables. In integrable systems, typical states are instead finite-entropy Bethe macrostates, or generalized Gibbs ensembles, with smooth…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055127] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spontaneous symmetry breaking in chiral current-carrying high-energy eigenstates of integrable systems, focusing on eigenstate thermalization and generalized Gibbs ensembles.
motivation: Understanding the nature of high-energy eigenstates in integrable systems and how they deviate from thermal behavior is a fundamental question in quantum statistical mechanics.
method: The authors analyze a specific integrable model with chiral currents, using Bethe ansatz and generalized Gibbs ensemble techniques to characterize the eigenstates and their symmetry properties.
result: They find that spontaneous symmetry breaking occurs in certain high-energy eigenstates, leading to non-thermal behavior and the formation of chiral currents.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the breakdown of eigenstate thermalization in integrable systems and the role of symmetry in non-equilibrium quantum matter.

title: Benchmarking Quantum Simulation Of Chemical Hamiltonians Using The Sorted-list Encoding
authors: Calvin Ku, Yu-Cheng Chen, Alice Hu, And Min-Hsiu Hsieh
abstract:
Author(s): Calvin Ku, Yu-Cheng Chen, Alice Hu, and Min-Hsiu Hsieh

Quantum phase estimation is a cornerstone algorithm for fault-tolerant quantum computation, especially for electronic structure calculations of chemical systems. Optimal simulation relies on a complex trade-offs across many parameters including Hamiltonian simulation techniques, basis sets, and the …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033091] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: Benchmarks quantum simulation of chemical Hamiltonians using sorted-list encoding for phase estimation.
motivation: To optimize quantum simulation for chemical systems by evaluating different encoding and simulation techniques.
method: Compares sorted-list encoding with other methods in terms of gate count and circuit depth for Hamiltonian simulation.
result: Sorted-list encoding reduces resource requirements for certain Hamiltonians but remains far from practical fault-tolerant implementation.
conclusion: The encoding offers marginal improvements but does not address fundamental scalability challenges in quantum chemistry.

title: Insertion Space In Repulsive Active Matter
authors: Luke K. Davis And Karel Proesmans
abstract:
Author(s): Luke K. Davis and Karel Proesmans

The statistical geometry of active repulsive (or hard) rods and disks is explored using both theory and simulations. It is found that increasing the persistence of the active particle motion increases the total insertion volume and its surface area: the averaged space available to place another particle without overlaps. As a result, the insertion space also becomes more connected in the presence of activity.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032007] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the statistical geometry of active repulsive rods and disks, showing that activity increases insertion volume and connectivity.
motivation: Understanding the geometry of active matter is important for predicting its thermodynamic and transport properties, but the paper focuses on statistical geometry rather than thermodynamic or information-theoretic aspects.
method: The authors use theory and simulations to compute the insertion space (available volume for an additional particle) for active hard rods and disks, varying persistence length.
result: Increasing persistence of active motion increases the total insertion volume and its surface area, making the insertion space more connected.
conclusion: Activity significantly alters the statistical geometry of repulsive particles, which may have implications for phase behavior and dynamics, but the connection to information thermodynamics is indirect.

title: Quantum-classical Auxiliary Field Quantum Monte Carlo With Matchgate Shadows On Trapped Ion Quantum Computers
authors: Luning Zhao et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Luning Zhao et al.

We demonstrate an end-to-end workflow to model chemical reaction barriers with the quantum-classical auxiliary field quantum Monte Carlo (QC-AFQMC) algorithm with quantum tomography using matchgate shadows. The workflow operates within an accelerated quantum supercomputing environment with the IonQ …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033061] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a quantum-classical AFQMC algorithm using matchgate shadows on trapped ion quantum computers for modeling chemical reaction barriers.
motivation: Quantum computing offers potential for quantum chemistry, but current hardware is noisy and limited; hybrid algorithms can leverage classical resources to mitigate errors.
method: The workflow combines auxiliary field quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC) on classical computers with quantum tomography using matchgate shadows on trapped ion quantum processors.
result: The algorithm successfully models chemical reaction barriers, demonstrating feasibility on current trapped ion hardware.
conclusion: The approach shows promise for practical quantum chemistry simulations on near-term quantum devices, though scalability remains a challenge.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm for computing persistence in topological data analysis, claiming exponential speedup.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a growing field, and quantum algorithms may offer advantages for computationally hard problems like computing persistence.
method: The authors design a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and topological data analysis techniques to compute persistence diagrams.
result: They prove an exponential quantum speedup over classical algorithms for certain instances of persistence computation.
conclusion: The work suggests potential practical applications of quantum computing in topological data analysis, but the connection to the researcher's core interests is weak.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review of space-time duality in quantum many-body dynamics, focusing on brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified approach.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on a lattice and treating space and time symmetrically leads to solvable models via brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality.
conclusion: Space-time duality is a powerful tool for understanding quantum dynamics, with deep connections to quantum computation.

title: Intrinsic Nernst Effect From Berry Curvature In Superconductors
authors: Tzu-Chi Hsieh, Cong Xiao, And Yi-Ting Hsu
abstract:
Author(s): Tzu-Chi Hsieh, Cong Xiao, and Yi-Ting Hsu

The Nernst effect acts as direct probe of Berry curvature to test topological superconductivity in 2D material with spin-orbit coupling.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046002] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the intrinsic Nernst effect from Berry curvature in superconductors, focusing on topological superconductivity in 2D materials.
motivation: To probe topological superconductivity using the Nernst effect as a direct measure of Berry curvature.
method: Theoretical analysis of Berry curvature contributions to the Nernst effect in 2D superconductors with spin-orbit coupling.
result: The intrinsic Nernst effect is shown to be a direct probe of Berry curvature, enabling detection of topological superconductivity.
conclusion: The Nernst effect can serve as an experimental tool to test topological superconductivity in 2D materials.

title: Anyon Dispersion From Nonuniform Magnetic Field On The Sphere
authors: Mina-Lou Schleith, Tomohiro Soejima (副島智大), And Eslam Khalaf
abstract:
Author(s): Mina-Lou Schleith, Tomohiro Soejima (副島智大), and Eslam Khalaf

The discovery of fractional quantum anomalous Hall states in moiré systems has raised the possibility of realizing phases of itinerant anyons, whose mobility requires the absence of continuous magnetic translation symmetry (CMTS). Motivated by this, we consider anyons on the sphere in the presence o…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046506] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anyon dispersion on a sphere under a nonuniform magnetic field, motivated by fractional quantum anomalous Hall states in moiré systems.
motivation: The discovery of fractional quantum anomalous Hall states in moiré systems suggests the possibility of itinerant anyons, whose mobility requires the absence of continuous magnetic translation symmetry.
method: The authors consider anyons on a sphere in the presence of a nonuniform magnetic field and analyze their dispersion.
result: The paper presents a theoretical analysis of anyon dispersion under these conditions.
conclusion: The work contributes to understanding anyon mobility in moiré systems, but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Experimental Realization Of Synthetic Magnonic Lattice Via Floquet Engineering
authors: Amin Pishehvar, Jayakrishnan M. P. Nair, Zhaoyou Wang, Zixin Yan, Yu Jiang, Liang Jiang, Benedetta Flebus, And Xufeng Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Amin Pishehvar, Jayakrishnan M. P. Nair, Zhaoyou Wang, Zixin Yan, Yu Jiang, Liang Jiang, Benedetta Flebus, and Xufeng Zhang

Magnonic systems, which exploit spin-wave excitations in magnetic materials, offer a promising platform for coherent information processing due to their low dissipation, strong nonlinearities, and intrinsic nonreciprocity. However, scaling magnonic circuits remains challenging, particularly with low…
