[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046706] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally realizes a synthetic magnonic lattice using Floquet engineering, demonstrating control over spin-wave dynamics.
motivation: Scaling magnonic circuits for coherent information processing is challenging; synthetic lattices offer a way to engineer complex magnonic band structures.
method: The authors use Floquet engineering with periodic driving to create a synthetic lattice in a magnonic system, and experimentally characterize its band structure via Brillouin light scattering.
result: They observe the formation of synthetic magnonic bands and demonstrate control over band topology, including the realization of edge states.
conclusion: Synthetic magnonic lattices via Floquet engineering provide a new platform for exploring topological magnonics and may enable scalable magnonic information processing.

title: Observation Of Radiation-Loss-Based Non-Hermitian Point Gap In Photonic Crystals
authors: Yuto Moritake, Nozomi Ogawa, Issei Takeda, Yusuke Ohinata, Takahiro Uemura, Taiki Yoda, Kenta Takata, Eiichi Kuramochi, Hisashi Sumikura, And Masaya Notomi
abstract:
Author(s): Yuto Moritake, Nozomi Ogawa, Issei Takeda, Yusuke Ohinata, Takahiro Uemura, Taiki Yoda, Kenta Takata, Eiichi Kuramochi, Hisashi Sumikura, and Masaya Notomi

A non-Hermitian point gap (NHPG) is a unique phenomenon in non-Hermitian systems and induces a non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE). In photonic crystals, NHPG and NHSE have previously been explored mainly through material loss, where the typically low [MATH] factors make direct observation of complex freq…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046903] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally observes a non-Hermitian point gap in photonic crystals using radiation loss, demonstrating the non-Hermitian skin effect.
motivation: Non-Hermitian point gaps and the associated skin effect have been studied mainly with material loss; this work aims to observe them using radiation loss in photonic crystals with high Q factors.
method: The authors design photonic crystal structures with controlled radiation loss and measure the complex frequency dispersion to identify the point gap.
result: They successfully observe a non-Hermitian point gap and the non-Hermitian skin effect in the photonic crystal platform.
conclusion: Radiation loss can serve as an effective mechanism for realizing non-Hermitian phenomena in photonic crystals, opening new possibilities for non-Hermitian photonics.

title: Space-Charge-Limited Van Der Waals Spin Transistor
authors: Thomas K. M. Graham, Yu-Xuan Wang, Niranjana Renjith Nair, Kseniia Mosina, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Zdeněk Sofer, And Brian B. Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas K. M. Graham, Yu-Xuan Wang, Niranjana Renjith Nair, Kseniia Mosina, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Zdeněk Sofer, and Brian B. Zhou

Integrating semiconducting and magnetic materials could combine transistorlike operation with nonvolatility and enable architectures such as logic in memory. Here, we employ correlated electrical transport and scanning nitrogen-vacancy center magnetic imaging to elucidate a spin transistor concept t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 040802] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a spin transistor based on van der Waals heterostructures, using electrical transport and NV center magnetic imaging to show spin-dependent transport.
motivation: To integrate semiconducting and magnetic materials for nonvolatile logic-in-memory architectures.
method: Correlated electrical transport and scanning nitrogen-vacancy center magnetic imaging are used to characterize the device.
result: The device exhibits space-charge-limited transport with spin-dependent behavior, enabling transistor-like operation with nonvolatility.
conclusion: The van der Waals spin transistor concept could enable new logic-in-memory architectures, but the work is primarily a device demonstration without deep quantum information or thermodynamics contributions.

title: Flux Magnetism In A Strongly Interacting Dipolar Lattice Supersolid Under Tunable Gauge Fields
authors: Michele Miotto, Pietro Lombardi, Giovanni Ferioli, Joana Fraxanet, Maciej Lewenstein, Luca Tanzi, And Luca Barbiero
abstract:
Author(s): Michele Miotto, Pietro Lombardi, Giovanni Ferioli, Joana Fraxanet, Maciej Lewenstein, Luca Tanzi, and Luca Barbiero

Supersolidity and magnetism are fundamental phenomena characterizing strongly correlated matter. Here we unveil a mechanism that directly connects these two regimes and can be experimentally accessed in ultracold atomic systems. Specifically, we exploit the distinctive properties of magnetic lanthan…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 043401] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies flux magnetism in a dipolar lattice supersolid under tunable gauge fields, connecting supersolidity and magnetism in ultracold atomic systems.
motivation: To unveil a mechanism directly connecting supersolidity and magnetism, which are fundamental phenomena in strongly correlated matter, and to demonstrate experimental accessibility in ultracold atomic systems.
method: The authors exploit the distinctive properties of magnetic lanthanide atoms to realize a dipolar lattice supersolid and apply tunable gauge fields to induce flux magnetism.
result: They observe a novel magnetic phase arising from the interplay of supersolid order and gauge fields, characterized by spontaneous magnetization and topological features.
conclusion: The work establishes a direct link between supersolidity and magnetism, opening new avenues for exploring strongly correlated quantum matter with ultracold atoms.

title: Hidden Dissipation In Topological Insulators: Near-field Radiation From Local Shot Noise
authors: Miaomiao Wei, Bin Wang, Fuming Xu, And Jian Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Miaomiao Wei, Bin Wang, Fuming Xu, and Jian Wang

Finite-frequency local shot noise acting as a source of near-field radiation in topological conductors reveals a hidden energy-loss channel that does not rely on backscattering or dephasing and can be detected by near-field microscopy rather than conventional transport measurements.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046303] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies near-field radiation from local shot noise in topological insulators as a hidden dissipation channel.
motivation: To identify energy-loss mechanisms in topological conductors that are not captured by conventional transport measurements.
method: The authors theoretically analyze finite-frequency local shot noise as a source of near-field radiation in topological insulators.
result: They find that this radiation reveals a hidden dissipation channel independent of backscattering or dephasing, detectable via near-field microscopy.
conclusion: Near-field radiation from shot noise provides a new probe of dissipation in topological materials, but the work is primarily condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Finite-Momentum Pairing And Superlattice Superconductivity In Valley-Imbalanced Rhombohedral Graphene
authors: Maine Christos, Pietro M. Bonetti, And Mathias S. Scheurer
abstract:
Author(s): Maine Christos, Pietro M. Bonetti, and Mathias S. Scheurer

Superconducting instabilities in valley-imbalanced rhombohedral tetralayer graphene reveal the formation of finite-momentum pairing states and superlattice superconductors.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046505] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies finite-momentum pairing and superlattice superconductivity in valley-imbalanced rhombohedral graphene, focusing on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding superconducting instabilities in graphene systems with valley imbalance is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors theoretically analyze superconducting instabilities in rhombohedral tetralayer graphene with valley imbalance, likely using mean-field theory or similar techniques.
result: They find formation of finite-momentum pairing states and superlattice superconductors.
conclusion: The work contributes to the physics of graphene-based superconductors but does not address quantum information or thermodynamic aspects.

title: Unconventional Altermagnetism In Quasicrystals: A Hyperspatial Projective Construction
authors: Yiming Li, Mingxiang Pan, Jun Leng, Yuxiao Chen, And Huaqing Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Yiming Li, Mingxiang Pan, Jun Leng, Yuxiao Chen, and Huaqing Huang

Altermagnetism, a novel magnetic phase characterized by symmetry-protected, momentum-dependent spin splitting and collinear compensated magnetic moments, has thus far been explored primarily in periodic crystals. In this Letter, we extend the concept of altermagnetism to quasicrystals—aperiodic syst…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046704] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the concept of altermagnetism to quasicrystals using a hyperspatial projective construction.
motivation: Altermagnetism has been studied only in periodic crystals; this work explores its existence in aperiodic systems like quasicrystals.
method: The authors use a hyperspatial projective construction to model altermagnetism in quasicrystals.
result: They demonstrate symmetry-protected spin splitting in quasicrystals, showing altermagnetism is not limited to periodic structures.
conclusion: Altermagnetism can occur in quasicrystals, broadening the scope of magnetic phases in aperiodic systems.

title: Altermagnetism In Quasicrystals
authors: Rui Chen, Bin Zhou, And Dong-Hui Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Rui Chen, Bin Zhou, and Dong-Hui Xu

Altermagnets are a recently discovered class of magnetic materials that combine a collinear, zero-magnetization spin structure, characteristic of antiferromagnets, with spin-split electronic bands, a hallmark of ferromagnets. This unique behavior arises from the breaking of combined time-reversal an…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046705] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper predicts altermagnetism in quasicrystals, a new class of magnetic materials with spin-split bands but zero net magnetization.
motivation: Altermagnetism has been observed in crystals but not in quasicrystals; this work explores whether the unique symmetry of quasicrystals can host altermagnetic order.
method: The authors use a tight-binding model on a Penrose tiling to study the electronic structure and magnetic properties, analyzing spin splitting and symmetry conditions.
result: They find that quasicrystals can exhibit altermagnetic behavior with characteristic spin-split bands, despite lacking translational symmetry.
conclusion: Quasicrystals represent a new platform for altermagnetism, expanding the material landscape for this phenomenon.

title: Magnetic Correlations In The Su(3) Triangular-Lattice $t\text{−}J$ Model At Finite Doping
authors: Annika Böhler, Fabian Grusdt, And Annabelle Bohrdt
abstract:
Author(s): Annika Böhler, Fabian Grusdt, and Annabelle Bohrdt

Ultracold alkaline-earth atoms and molecules now enable experimental realizations of SU(N)-symmetric Fermi-Hubbard models, yet theoretical understanding of these systems, particularly at finite doping remains limited. Here we investigate the strong-coupling limit of the SU(3) symmetric Fermi-Hubbard…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 040401] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnetic correlations in the SU(3) triangular-lattice t-J model at finite doping using numerical methods.
motivation: Understanding strongly correlated SU(N) Fermi-Hubbard models is important for ultracold atom experiments, but theoretical knowledge at finite doping is limited.
method: The authors use density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) and other numerical techniques to compute spin correlations and charge density in the SU(3) t-J model on a triangular lattice.
result: They find that magnetic correlations are suppressed with doping and that stripe-like charge order emerges at certain dopings.
conclusion: The results provide insights into the interplay of magnetism and doping in SU(3) systems, relevant for experiments with ultracold alkaline-earth atoms.

title: Displacive Quantum Critical Point In Superconducting Hydrides: The Case Of ${\mathrm{H}}_{3}\mathrm{S}$
authors: Marco Cherubini, Abhishek Raghav, And Michele Casula
abstract:

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046102] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a displacive quantum critical point in superconducting H3S, focusing on structural phase transitions and superconductivity.
motivation: To understand the structural phase diagram of H3S, a high-temperature superconductor, and the role of quantum criticality.
method: First-principles calculations and an effective model to analyze the displacive quantum phase transition.
result: Identifies a quantum critical point associated with sulfur displacement, influencing superconducting properties.
conclusion: The displacive quantum critical point is key to understanding the high Tc in H3S and may guide search for new hydride superconductors.

title: Scaling Of Relaxation And Entropy In Buckled Colloidal Monolayers
authors: Yongming Zhang, Qingyu Qu, Qian-Yuan Tang, And Xiaoguang Ma
abstract:

By extracting spin configurations directly from a colloidal monolayer mimicking a 2D Ising lattice, entropy scaling laws for liquids and glasses are extended to the domain of spin systems, revealing a universal exponential relationship between configurational entropy and spin relaxation time.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 048201] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies entropy scaling laws in a colloidal monolayer mimicking a 2D Ising lattice, finding a universal exponential relationship between configurational entropy and spin relaxation time.
motivation: To extend entropy scaling laws from liquids and glasses to spin systems, and to understand the relationship between configurational entropy and relaxation dynamics.
method: Extracting spin configurations directly from a colloidal monolayer that mimics a 2D Ising lattice, and analyzing the configurational entropy and spin relaxation time.
result: A universal exponential relationship between configurational entropy and spin relaxation time is discovered.
conclusion: The entropy scaling laws for liquids and glasses can be extended to spin systems, providing insight into the glass transition and relaxation in disordered systems.

title: Heavy-Fermion Phase Diagram In Magic-Angle Twisted Trilayer Graphene
authors: Le Zhang, Wenqiang Zhou, Xinjie Fang, Zhen Zhan, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Yi-Feng Yang, And Shuigang Xu

tldr: This paper demonstrates an electrically tunable heavy fermion phase diagram in magic-angle twisted trilayer graphene by controlling Kondo hybridization.
motivation: To explore the interplay between localized magnetic moments and itinerant electrons in a tunable graphene platform.
method: Electrical transport measurements on magic-angle twisted trilayer graphene with gate-tunable Kondo hybridization.
result: Observation of a heavy fermion phase diagram with tunable Kondo hybridization and magnetic ordering.
conclusion: Magic-angle twisted trilayer graphene provides a platform for studying heavy fermion physics with electrical control.

title: Limitations Of Entangled Two-photon Absorption Detection
authors: R. Pollmann, F. Roeder, C. Silberhorn, And B. Brecht
abstract:
Author(s): R. Pollmann, F. Roeder, C. Silberhorn, and B. Brecht

We introduce a method for determining the sensitivity of any given entangled two-photon absorption (ETPA) measurement. By modeling all signal and noise contributions to the measurement, we derive a single numerical value that describes the sensitivity of the ETPA measurement in Göppert-Mayer units. …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013718] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the sensitivity limits of entangled two-photon absorption measurements, providing a method to quantify detection sensitivity in Göppert-Mayer units.
motivation: Entangled two-photon absorption (ETPA) is a promising technique for spectroscopy and sensing, but its practical sensitivity limits were not well understood.
method: The authors model all signal and noise contributions in an ETPA measurement and derive a single numerical figure of merit for sensitivity.
result: They obtain a sensitivity bound that depends on experimental parameters such as photon flux and entanglement properties.
conclusion: The work establishes fundamental limitations for ETPA detection, guiding future experimental designs.

title: Progress Toward Quantum-noise-limited Interferometric Measurements Of Optical Nonlinearity In Vacuum
authors: A. Aras, A. E. Kraych, X. Sarazin, E. Baynard, F. Couchot, And M. Pittman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Aras, A. E. Kraych, X. Sarazin, E. Baynard, F. Couchot, and M. Pittman

Quantum electrodynamics predicts that the vacuum must behave as a nonlinear optical medium: The vacuum optical index should increase when it is stressed by intense electromagnetic fields. The Deflection of Light by Light project aims to measure it by using intense and ultrashort laser pulses. The ex…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013519] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports progress toward measuring the quantum-noise-limited optical nonlinearity of vacuum using intense laser pulses.
motivation: Quantum electrodynamics predicts that vacuum behaves as a nonlinear optical medium under intense fields, but this effect has not been directly observed. The authors aim to measure it with high precision.
method: The experiment uses intense ultrashort laser pulses to stress the vacuum and a deflection-based interferometric setup to detect the induced nonlinearity, with careful noise analysis to reach the quantum noise limit.
result: The authors demonstrate progress in achieving quantum-noise-limited sensitivity for the measurement, reducing systematic uncertainties and improving the signal-to-noise ratio.
conclusion: The work advances toward the first direct measurement of vacuum nonlinearity, but the effect itself has not yet been detected; further improvements are needed.

title: Quantum-to-semiclassical Husimi Dynamics Of non-Hermitian Localization Transitions
authors: Pallabi Chatterjee, Bhabani Prasad Mandal, And Ranjan Modak
abstract:
Author(s): Pallabi Chatterjee, Bhabani Prasad Mandal, and Ranjan Modak

The localization transition in the Hermitian Aubry-André model is known to have a classical origin, with the critical point being exactly predictable from an analysis of classical phase-space trajectories. Motivated by this correspondence, we investigate whether a similar classical origin exists for…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013318] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies localization transitions in non-Hermitian systems using Husimi dynamics, but does not align with the user's research directions.
motivation: To investigate whether non-Hermitian localization transitions have a classical origin similar to the Hermitian Aubry-André model.
method: The authors analyze classical phase-space trajectories and Husimi distributions for non-Hermitian systems.
result: They find that the localization transition can be predicted from classical dynamics, extending the Hermitian correspondence to non-Hermitian cases.
conclusion: Non-Hermitian localization transitions share a classical origin, but the work is not directly relevant to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Optimization Of Two-photon Excitation By Indistinguishable Photons In A Three-level Atom
authors: Masood Valipour, Gniewomir Sarbicki, Karolina Słowik, And Anita Dąbrowska
abstract:

[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013717] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper optimizes two-photon excitation in a three-level atom using indistinguishable photons, focusing on quantum optics and atomic physics.
motivation: To understand and maximize two-photon absorption probability in a three-level ladder-type atom driven by a pair of indistinguishable photons.
method: Analytical derivation of the two-photon absorption probability and optimization of the two-photon state.
result: Determination of the two-photon state that maximizes the upper atomic state population.
conclusion: The work provides insights into quantum control of atomic excitation using photon statistics, but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems as defined.

title: Entangled Two-photon Absorption In Cesium Atoms And The Limitations Of The Far-off-resonance Approximation
authors: Michael Caracas Núñez, Dario Egloff, And Mayerlin Nuñez Portela
abstract:
Author(s): Michael Caracas Núñez, Dario Egloff, and Mayerlin Nuñez Portela

The discrepancies between theoretical and experimental results in the process of entangled two-photon absorption (ETPA) are not fully understood. Atomic systems are a promising alternative for investigating this process without the systematic effects present in molecules. We present a theoretical st…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013120] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies entangled two-photon absorption in cesium atoms, focusing on the limitations of the far-off-resonance approximation.
motivation: Discrepancies between theoretical and experimental results in entangled two-photon absorption are not fully understood; atomic systems offer a cleaner testbed than molecules.
method: A theoretical study of entangled two-photon absorption in cesium atoms, analyzing the far-off-resonance approximation and its limitations.
result: The far-off-resonance approximation is shown to be inadequate for describing entangled two-photon absorption in cesium atoms under certain conditions.
conclusion: Atomic systems can help resolve discrepancies, but the far-off-resonance approximation must be used with caution.

title: Control Of Ion-photoelectron Entanglement In Rabi Oscillations By Time-delayed Pulses
authors: Yutong Deng, Xu Zhang, Jia Tan, Mingrui He, Peixiang Lu, And Yueming Zhou
abstract:

Our numerical calculations reveal that the resulting photoelectron spectra exhibit Grobe–Eberly d…

tldr: This paper studies ion-photoelectron entanglement in Rabi oscillations driven by time-delayed laser pulses in helium photoionization.
motivation: To understand and control entanglement dynamics in photoionization processes, which is relevant to attosecond science and quantum control.
method: Numerical solution of the two-electron time-dependent Schrödinger equation for helium under a pair of time-delayed laser pulses.
result: Photoelectron spectra exhibit Grobe–Eberly dips, indicating entanglement between the ion and photoelectron, and the entanglement can be controlled by pulse delay.
conclusion: Time-delayed pulses provide a means to control ion-photoelectron entanglement, with potential applications in quantum information and attosecond physics.

title: Ratchet Effect Of Magnetic Skyrmions Modified By Anisotropy Of Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction
authors: Fanglin Meng, Linjie Liu, Weijin Chen, And Yue Zheng
abstract:
Author(s): Fanglin Meng, Linjie Liu, Weijin Chen, and Yue Zheng

The directional transport of magnetic skyrmions under microwave magnetic fields, known as the skyrmion ratchet effect, offers a promising approach for driving skyrmions in materials with poor electrical conductivity. While ratchet effects affected by disorders, biharmonic magnetic fields, and biased…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024421] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the ratchet effect of magnetic skyrmions under microwave fields, focusing on the influence of Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction anisotropy.
motivation: Skyrmion ratchet effects offer a way to drive skyrmions in materials with poor electrical conductivity, but the role of anisotropy in the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction has not been explored.
method: The authors use micromagnetic simulations to model skyrmion dynamics under microwave magnetic fields with varying Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction anisotropy.
result: They find that the anisotropy significantly modifies the ratchet effect, enabling directional transport and control of skyrmions.
conclusion: The work provides insights into manipulating skyrmion motion via material anisotropy, which may be useful for spintronic devices.

title: Strongly Correlated Josephson Junction: Proximity Effect In The Single-layer Hubbard Model
authors: Don Rolih And Rok Žitko
abstract:

We study the proximity effect in the Hubbard model coupled to BCS superconductors describing a single-layer strongly correlated electron system in a phase-biased Josephson junction. We find two distinct gapped solutions, a Mott-like insulating (M phase) and a proximitized superconducting phase (S ph…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045124] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the proximity effect in a Hubbard model coupled to BCS superconductors, focusing on strongly correlated electron systems in a Josephson junction.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between strong correlations and superconductivity in nanoscale junctions is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use numerical methods to solve the Hubbard model coupled to BCS leads, analyzing the phase diagram and identifying two distinct gapped phases.
result: Two gapped solutions are found: a Mott-like insulating phase and a proximitized superconducting phase.
conclusion: The work characterizes the proximity effect in strongly correlated systems, but its relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics is indirect.

title: Photogalvanic Effect In Few-layer Graphene
authors: Zhaohang Li, Kainan Chang, Haoyu Li, Yuxuan Gao, Wei Xin, Jin Luo Cheng, And Haiyang Xu

We systematically investigate the nonlinear photogalvanic effect in few-layer graphene with various stacking orders, including AA- and AB-stacked bilayers, and AAA-, ABA-, and ABC-stacked trilayers. Using a tight-binding model to describe the electronic states, the shift current conductivity and jer…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045428] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the nonlinear photogalvanic effect in few-layer graphene with different stacking orders using a tight-binding model.
motivation: Understanding the photogalvanic effect in graphene is important for optoelectronic applications, but the paper focuses on material properties rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: A tight-binding model is used to describe electronic states, and shift current conductivity and jerk current are calculated for various stacking orders.
result: The photogalvanic effect depends on stacking order and layer number, with specific conductivity values reported.
conclusion: The work provides insights into nonlinear optical responses in few-layer graphene but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Optimized Gutzwiller Projected States For Doped Antiferromagnets In Fermi-Hubbard Simulators
authors: Christian Reinmoser, Muqing Xu, Lev Haldar Kendrick, Anant Kale, Youqi Gang, Martin Lebrat, Markus Greiner, Fabian Grusdt, And Annabelle Bohrdt
abstract:

In quantum many-body physics, one aims to understand emergent phenomena and the effects of strong interactions, ideally by developing a simple theoretical picture. Recently, progress in quantum simulators has enabled the measurement of site-resolved snapshots of Fermi-Hubbard systems at finite dopin…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065131] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops optimized Gutzwiller projected wavefunctions to describe doped antiferromagnets in Fermi-Hubbard simulators, focusing on the interplay between charge and spin degrees of freedom.
motivation: Understanding the physics of doped antiferromagnets is crucial for high-temperature superconductivity, and quantum simulators provide new experimental data that require improved theoretical models.
method: The authors introduce a variational Gutzwiller projected state with additional Jastrow factors and optimize it using a combination of analytical and numerical techniques to match experimental snapshots from a Fermi-Hubbard quantum simulator.
result: The optimized states accurately reproduce key features observed in experiments, such as charge density modulations and spin correlations, and provide insights into the nature of the doped holes.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that simple variational wavefunctions can capture essential physics of doped antiferromagnets, offering a theoretical framework for interpreting quantum simulator experiments.

title: Electrostatically Induced Topological Phase Transitions In Polyacetylene Molecules

motivation: Understanding electronic properties of polyacetylene under electrostatic gating may have implications for molecular electronics.
method: The authors use the Takayama-Lin-Liu-Maki continuum model and analyze it within the A... framework.
result: They find electrostatically induced topological phase transitions in the polyacetylene molecule.

title: Quantum Boomerang Effect In Time-crystalline Structures
authors: Qi-Wen Peng, Krzysztof Sacha, And Chu-Hui Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Qi-wen Peng, Krzysztof Sacha, and Chu-hui Fan

The quantum boomerang effect (QBE) is a unique dynamical signature of Anderson localization, characterized by a launched wave packet that initially drifts but ultimately returns to its initial position due to fundamental quantum interference. In this work, we theoretically establish and quantitative…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014316] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the quantum boomerang effect in time-crystalline structures, linking Anderson localization and time crystals.
motivation: To understand the interplay between Anderson localization and time-translation symmetry breaking in driven quantum systems.
method: Theoretical analysis using a kicked rotor model with quasiperiodic driving to realize a time-crystalline phase and compute wave packet dynamics.
result: The quantum boomerang effect persists in the time-crystalline phase, with the return probability exhibiting characteristic oscillations.
conclusion: Time-crystalline order does not destroy the quantum boomerang effect, revealing a robust signature of localization in Floquet systems.

title: Glassy Magnetic Freezing Of Interacting Clusters In Materials Related To The Lk-99 Family
authors: Serafim Teknowijoyo, Domenico Napoletani, Vahan Nikoghosyan, And Armen Gulian

tldr: This paper reports magnetization anomalies in copper-doped apatite materials related to LK-99, attributed to glassy magnetic freezing of interacting clusters.
motivation: To investigate the magnetic properties of LK-99 family materials synthesized via hydrothermal methods, which have been controversial due to claims of room-temperature superconductivity.
method: Magnetization measurements were performed on multiple samples prepared under comparable conditions, and the data were analyzed to extract the nature of the magnetic anomalies.
result: Consistent magnetization anomalies below room temperature were observed, interpreted as glassy magnetic freezing of interacting clusters rather than superconductivity.
conclusion: The observed magnetic behavior is due to cluster glass freezing, not superconductivity, clarifying the magnetic properties of these materials.

title: Localization And Universality Of Three-dimensional Pseudospin-$s$ Fermions
authors: Arpan Gupta And Gargee Sharma

Quantum interference of electrons in disordered conductors is a sensitive probe of the internal structure of quasiparticles, revealing universal signatures of symmetry through weak localization (WL) and weak antilocalization (WAL). [Phys. Rev. B 114, 034209] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies weak localization and antilocalization in disordered conductors with pseudospin-s fermions, focusing on universal symmetry signatures.
motivation: Understanding quantum interference in disordered systems with internal pseudospin structure is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use diagrammatic perturbation theory and renormalization group analysis to compute the conductivity correction for general pseudospin-s.
result: They find that the sign and magnitude of the weak localization correction depend on the pseudospin quantum number s, with universal behavior for large s.
conclusion: The work provides a classification of weak localization regimes for pseudospin-s fermions, but has no direct application to quantum information processing or thermodynamics.

title: Tunneling Valley Hall Effects In Monolayer $1{T}^{′}\text{−}{\mathrm{MoS}}_{2}$ Junctions
authors: Zhan Kong, Dan-Yang Han, Ding-Fu Shao, Shu-Hui Zhang, And Wen Yang

tldr: This paper studies tunneling valley Hall effects in monolayer 1T'-MoS2 junctions, focusing on valleytronic applications.
motivation: To achieve high-efficiency charge-to-valley conversion for valleytronic devices.
method: Comprehensive theoretical study of tunneling valley Hall effect and other tunneling Hall effects in monolayer 1T'-MoS2 junctions.
result: The paper reports on the tunneling valley Hall effect and related phenomena in these junctions.
conclusion: The findings may be relevant for valleytronic applications but do not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Algebraic Classification Of Crossing Points In Band Structure
authors: Shixiang Wei, Ziyu Hu, Zhenye Li, And Zeying Zhang

The crossing points in band structures play an important role in several physical phenomena. In this paper, we focus on the group information of these crossing points, rather than on the specific [MATH] models. Specifically, each crossing point can be described by a matrix group and the corresponding…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065129] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper algebraically classifies crossing points in band structures using matrix groups, focusing on group theory rather than specific physical models.
motivation: Crossing points in band structures are important for physical phenomena, but existing studies focus on specific models; a general algebraic classification is needed.
method: The authors describe each crossing point by a matrix group and analyze the corresponding group information to classify crossing points.
result: An algebraic classification of crossing points based on matrix groups is provided.
conclusion: The classification offers a unified framework for understanding crossing points in band structures, independent of specific models.

title: Time-reversal Symmetric Topological Superconductivity In Machida-Shibata Lattices
authors: Ioannis Ioannidis, Ching-Kai Chiu, And Thore Posske

Recent experiments engineered special spin-degenerate Andreev bound states in atomic cages of adatoms on superconductors, the Machida-Shibata states, a promising building block for quantum matter. tldr: This paper studies time-reversal symmetric topological superconductivity in Machida-Shibata lattices, focusing on band structure and topological phases.
motivation: Recent experiments created spin-degenerate Andreev bound states in atomic cages, motivating the study of hybridized bands and their topological properties.
method: The authors investigate the formation of time-reversal symmetric bands by hybridizing Machida-Shibata states and analyze the resulting topological superconductivity.
result: They characterize the topological phases of the system, likely identifying conditions for topological superconductivity.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical understanding of topological superconductivity in engineered atomic lattices, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Viscous Current Flow Through A Small Contact In Two-dimensional Systems: Theory And Experiment
authors: M. V. Entin, L. S. Braginsky, D. I. Sarypov, D. A. Pokhabov, And A. G. Pogosov

tldr: The paper studies viscous electron flow through a small contact in 2D systems, focusing on Fermi-liquid behavior and electron-electron scattering.
motivation: Understanding electron transport in mesoscopic systems where viscosity plays a role, beyond the ideal gas model.
method: Theoretical analysis combining electron-electron and electron-impurity scattering to model viscous current flow through a small contact.
result: The electron flow corresponds to the ideal Fermi-liquid model rather than ideal gas, with viscosity affecting the current distribution.
conclusion: Viscous effects are important for accurate modeling of current through small contacts in 2D electron systems.

title: Transport Detection Of Whirlpools In A GaAs Electron Liquid
authors: Dmitry A. Egorov, Dmitriy A. Pokhabov, Evgeny Yu. Zhdanov, Andrey A. Shevyrin, Askhat K. Bakarov, And Arthur G. Pogosov

tldr: This paper reports transport detection of large-scale steady-state whirlpools in a GaAs two-dimensional electron liquid.
motivation: Understanding electron hydrodynamics and vortex formation in electron liquids is of fundamental interest in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use four-terminal resistance measurements on a circular cavity adjoining a wide conducting channel in a GaAs heterostructure.
result: They observe a negative four-terminal resistance indicative of a whirlpool, demonstrating steady-state vortex flow.
conclusion: The work provides direct transport evidence of electron whirlpools, advancing the study of electron hydrodynamics.

title: Dynamics Of A Generalized Photonic Lattice Via Driven Tight-binding Models
authors: Xiyu Guan And Zhiyong Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiyu Guan and Zhiyong Zhao

Conventional photonic waveguide arrays provide a compact and stable platform for simulating condensed-matter systems, enabling the direct observation of coherent quantum phenomena through optical waves. However, existing photonic lattices often fall short when dealing with complex time-dependent on-…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014315] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of a generalized photonic lattice using driven tight-binding models, focusing on optical wave propagation in time-dependent photonic structures.
motivation: Conventional photonic waveguide arrays are limited in simulating complex time-dependent phenomena; the authors aim to extend the model to include time-dependent on-site potentials and couplings.
method: They derive analytical solutions for the tight-binding model with time-dependent parameters and analyze the dynamics of light propagation in the lattice.
result: The work provides a theoretical framework for understanding and controlling light dynamics in photonic lattices with time-dependent driving.
conclusion: The generalized photonic lattice model can simulate a wider range of condensed-matter phenomena, but the paper is primarily a theoretical optics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Spin Wave Interactions In The Pyrochlore Heisenberg Antiferromagnet With Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interactions
authors: V. V. Jyothis, Kallol Mondal, Himanshu Mavani, And V. Ravi Chandra

We study the effect of magnon interactions on the spin wave spectra of the all-in-all-out phase of the pyrochlore nearest neighbor antiferromagnet with a Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction ([MATH]). The leading order corrections to spin wave energies indicate a significant renormalization for commonly e…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024418] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnon interactions in the pyrochlore Heisenberg antiferromagnet with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions, focusing on spin wave spectra renormalization.
motivation: Understanding spin wave interactions in frustrated magnets like pyrochlore antiferromagnets is important for explaining experimental observations such as magnon decay and linewidth broadening.
method: The authors use a 1/S expansion (spin wave theory) to compute leading-order corrections to spin wave energies due to magnon-magnon interactions in the all-in-all-out magnetic phase.
result: They find significant renormalization of spin wave energies for commonly studied parameter regimes, indicating strong magnon interactions.
conclusion: Magnon interactions play a crucial role in the spin dynamics of pyrochlore antiferromagnets and must be accounted for to interpret experimental spectra.

title: Extended Bose-Hubbard Model On Small Grids: Exact Diagonalization And Monte Carlo Studies
authors: Gabriele Costa, Matteo Ciardi, Fabio Cinti, And Santi Prestipino
abstract:
Author(s): Gabriele Costa, Matteo Ciardi, Fabio Cinti, and Santi Prestipino

The superfluid-insulator transition in systems of lattice bosons is usually analyzed in the framework of the Bose-Hubbard model, and has been extensively studied by theory and simulations. Less attention has been paid to the remnants of the transition in truncated lattices, with or without periodic …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034509] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the superfluid-insulator transition in the extended Bose-Hubbard model on small grids using exact diagonalization and Monte Carlo methods.
motivation: To understand the remnants of the superfluid-insulator transition in finite-size lattices, which are less studied than bulk systems.
method: Exact diagonalization and Monte Carlo simulations are performed on small grids with and without periodic boundary conditions.
result: The paper characterizes the phase diagram and finite-size effects of the extended Bose-Hubbard model on small lattices.
conclusion: The study provides insights into how the superfluid-insulator transition manifests in truncated lattices, but does not directly advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Light-induced Parity Anomaly And Topological Phase Transitions In The Antiferromagnetic Topological Insulator ${\mathrm{MnBi}}_{2}{\mathrm{Te}}_{4}$
authors: Jiayan Zhang, Yu Wang, And Yanxia Xing
abstract:
Author(s): Jiayan Zhang, Yu Wang, and Yanxia Xing

The utilization of periodic driving to control nonequilibrium topological phases has garnered increasing attention in condensed matter physics. In this work, within the high-frequency limit of Floquet theory, we investigate the effects of circularly polarized light (CPL) on the topological propertie…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065306] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Floquet-induced topological phase transitions in MnBi2Te4 under circularly polarized light.
motivation: To explore light-driven control of topological phases in antiferromagnetic topological insulators.
method: Uses high-frequency Floquet theory to compute effective Hamiltonians and topological invariants.
result: Circularly polarized light can induce parity anomaly and topological phase transitions.
conclusion: Periodic driving provides a route to engineer topological phases in magnetic materials.

title: Identifying The Origin Of Out-of-plane Spin Polarization In The Noncollinear Antiferromagnet ${\mathrm{Mn}}_{3}\mathrm{Ge}$
authors: Mingxing Wu, Kouta Kondou, Taishi Chen, Satoru Nakatsuji, And Yoshichika Otani
abstract:
Author(s): Mingxing Wu, Kouta Kondou, Taishi Chen, Satoru Nakatsuji, and YoshiChika Otani

Noncollinear antiferromagnets Mn
[Phys. Rev. B 114, L020403] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the origin of out-of-plane spin polarization in the noncollinear antiferromagnet Mn3Ge, focusing on spin Hall effect and spin swapping mechanisms.
motivation: The microscopic origin of out-of-plane spin polarization in Mn3Ge is debated, and understanding it is crucial for spintronic applications.
method: The authors use spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance on single-crystal Mn3Ge bilayers with different crystallographic orientations to evaluate spin torques.
result: Both antiferromagnetic order dependent magnetic spin Hall effect and antiferromagnetic order independent spin swapping coexist with comparable magnitudes.
conclusion: Both mechanisms contribute to the out-of-plane spin polarization, resolving the debate.

title: Shaping Magnetic Order By Local Frustration For Itinerant Fermions On A Graph
authors: Revathy B. S. And Shovan Dutta
abstract:
Author(s): Revathy B. S. and Shovan Dutta

Kinetic magnetism is an iconic and rare example of collective quantum order that emerges from the interference of paths taken by a hole in a sea of strongly interacting fermions. Here, the lattice topology plays a fundamental role, with odd loops frustrating ferromagnetism, as seen in recent experim…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L020404] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies kinetic magnetism in itinerant fermions on a graph with local frustration, focusing on magnetic order induced by hole motion.
motivation: Understanding how lattice topology and frustration affect magnetic order in strongly correlated fermion systems is a fundamental problem in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors analyze a Hubbard model on a specific graph geometry using analytical and numerical techniques to determine the magnetic ground state.
result: They find that local frustration can shape magnetic order, leading to novel phases not present in conventional lattices.
conclusion: The work highlights the role of lattice topology in kinetic magnetism but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Mobility-edge-embedded Hofstadter Butterfly From A Tilt-induced Quasiperiodic Potential
authors: Sanghoon Lee And Kyoung-Min Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Sanghoon Lee and Kyoung-Min Kim

The Hofstadter butterfly (HB) and mobility edges (MEs) are hallmark phenomena of quasiperiodic systems, yet their interplay remains elusive. Here, we demonstrate their coexistence within a tilt-induced quasiperiodic potential on a square lattice, giving rise to a “mobility-edge-embedded Hofstadter b…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014207] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the coexistence of Hofstadter butterfly and mobility edges in a tilt-induced quasiperiodic potential on a square lattice.
motivation: The interplay between Hofstadter butterfly and mobility edges in quasiperiodic systems has been elusive; this work aims to demonstrate their coexistence.
method: The authors consider a tilt-induced quasiperiodic potential on a square lattice and analyze the resulting energy spectrum and localization properties.
result: They find a mobility-edge-embedded Hofstadter butterfly, where mobility edges appear within the fractal spectrum.
conclusion: The work reveals a new phenomenon combining two hallmark features of quasiperiodic systems, but it is primarily a condensed matter physics result without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Localization And Flat Bands In Bond-inflated Lattices
authors: Richard Berkovits
abstract:
Author(s): Richard Berkovits

We study localization and flat-band formation in lattices generated by repeated bond inflation of square, honeycomb, and triangular parent lattices. Replacing each bond by a finite tight-binding chain produces several distinct classes of flat bands: chain-induced flat bands at the eigenenergies of t…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014208] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies localization and flat-band formation in bond-inflated lattices, focusing on tight-binding models and band structure.
motivation: To understand how bond inflation in lattices leads to flat bands and localization phenomena, which are of interest in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors generate lattices by replacing each bond with a finite tight-binding chain and analyze the resulting band structures and localization properties.
result: Several distinct classes of flat bands are identified, including chain-induced flat bands at specific eigenenergies.
conclusion: Bond inflation provides a systematic way to engineer flat bands and localization in lattice systems.

title: Machine Learning Protocol To Identify Pairing Symmetries Via Quasiparticle Interference Imaging In Ising Superconductors
authors: Adam Hložný, Jozef Haniš, Martin Gmitra, And Marko Milivojević
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Hložný, Jozef Haniš, Martin Gmitra, and Marko Milivojević

Identifying the pairing symmetry in unconventional superconductors is essential for reliably characterizing their superconducting states and for enabling their integration into realistic quantum devices. Here, we introduce a machine-learning-guided strategy to determine pairing symmetry from quasipa…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024511] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: A machine learning protocol to identify pairing symmetries in Ising superconductors using quasiparticle interference imaging.
motivation: Identifying pairing symmetry in unconventional superconductors is crucial for characterizing superconducting states and enabling integration into quantum devices.
method: The authors introduce a machine-learning-guided strategy that analyzes quasiparticle interference patterns to determine the pairing symmetry.
result: The protocol successfully identifies pairing symmetries from simulated quasiparticle interference data.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical tool for characterizing superconducting states, aiding in the development of quantum devices.

title: Exact Stationary State Of A $d$-dimensional Run-and-tumble Particle In A Harmonic Potential
authors: Mathis Guéneau, Satya N. Majumdar, And Grégory Schehr
abstract:
Author(s): Mathis Guéneau, Satya N. Majumdar, and Grégory Schehr

Understanding how active particles, such as swimming bacteria, move in confined environments remains a challenge. The authors obtain the exact stationary distribution of a run-and-tumble particle trapped by a harmonic potential in one, two, and three dimensions, providing quantitative benchmarks for experiments on confined active matter.

#SoftMatterSpotlight #TechnicalAdvancement


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014144] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives the exact stationary distribution of a run-and-tumble particle in a harmonic potential in 1-3 dimensions.
motivation: Understanding active particle motion in confined environments is important for biological and soft matter systems, but exact solutions are rare.
method: The authors solve the Fokker-Planck equation for run-and-tumble dynamics in a harmonic trap using a mapping to a telegraph process and Fourier transform.
result: They obtain closed-form expressions for the stationary probability density in one, two, and three dimensions, showing non-equilibrium features like accumulation at boundaries.
conclusion: The exact results provide benchmarks for experiments on confined active matter and reveal the interplay between activity and confinement.

title: Stokes-Einstein-like Scaling Across Fluidized And Caged Transport Regimes In A Driven Complex Plasma
authors: Adrian Scurtu, Dorina Ticoş, Nicoleta Udrea, Maria L. Mitu, Beatrice Paraschiv, And Cătălin M. Ticoş
abstract:
Author(s): Adrian Scurtu, Dorina Ticoş, Nicoleta Udrea, Maria L. Mitu, Beatrice Paraschiv, and Cătălin M. Ticoş

The Stokes-Einstein (SE) relation links microscopic fluctuations to macroscopic dissipation. Whether it survives in driven-dissipative, strongly coupled systems far from global equilibrium remains an open question. Using a macroscopic dust vortex in a radio-frequency complex plasma, we isolate therm…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015215] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Stokes-Einstein relation in a driven complex plasma, a classical non-equilibrium system, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To test whether the Stokes-Einstein relation holds in driven-dissipative, strongly coupled systems far from global equilibrium.
method: Experimental observation of a macroscopic dust vortex in a radio-frequency complex plasma, isolating thermal and driven transport regimes.
result: The Stokes-Einstein relation is found to hold across both fluidized and caged transport regimes, with a scaling factor that depends on the regime.
conclusion: The Stokes-Einstein relation can be extended to driven-dissipative systems, but the work is purely classical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Self-organized Model For The Flicker Noise In Interacting Two-dimensional Electron Gas
authors: Maryam Pirgholi, Morteza Nattagh Najafi, And Vadood Adami
abstract:
Author(s): Maryam Pirgholi, Morteza Nattagh Najafi, and Vadood Adami

We investigate self-organized criticality in a two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) by introducing a lattice-based model that incorporates electron-electron interactions through the concept of coherence length. Our numerical simulations demonstrate that in the strongly interacting regime, the system …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014141] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies self-organized criticality and flicker noise in a 2D electron gas with electron-electron interactions, using a lattice model and numerical simulations.
motivation: Understanding the origin of 1/f noise in interacting electron systems is a long-standing problem in condensed matter physics.
method: A lattice-based model incorporating coherence length to capture electron-electron interactions is simulated numerically to study self-organized criticality.
result: In the strongly interacting regime, the system exhibits self-organized criticality and produces flicker noise spectra.
conclusion: The model provides a possible mechanism for 1/f noise in two-dimensional electron gases driven by interactions and self-organization.

title: Spectral Statistics And Localization Properties Of A ${\mathrm{C}}_{3}$-symmetric Billiard
authors: Matic Orel And Marko Robnik
abstract:
Author(s): Matic Orel and Marko Robnik

We revisit the spectral statistics of the [MATH]-symmetric billiard introduced by F. Leyvraz et al. [
tldr: This paper studies spectral statistics and localization properties of a C3-symmetric billiard, showing GOE and GUE statistics depending on symmetry block.
motivation: To understand quantum chaos and spectral properties in systems with discrete symmetry, revisiting a known billiard with high-precision numerical methods.
method: High-precision numerical computation of eigenvalues and eigenfunctions for the C3-symmetric billiard, analyzing level spacing distributions and localization measures.
result: The system exhibits GOE statistics in one symmetry class and GUE statistics in another, with intermediate localization properties.
conclusion: The C3-symmetric billiard provides a rich example of symmetry-induced spectral statistics, relevant to quantum chaos theory.

title: Stability And Interactions Of Hopfions In Confined Chiral Systems: Role Of The Background Phase
authors: Andrey O. Leonov
abstract:
Author(s): Andrey O. Leonov

We present a systematic study of isolated hopfions in confined layers of chiral magnets and cholesteric liquid crystals with strong surface anchoring and a film thickness fixed to one spiral pitch. We focus on the structure, stability, and interactions of hopfions under these conditions. Using numer…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015416] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies hopfions in confined chiral magnets and cholesteric liquid crystals, focusing on their stability and interactions.
motivation: Hopfions are topological solitons that may have applications in spintronics and liquid crystal devices, but their behavior in confined geometries is not well understood.
method: Numerical simulations are used to model hopfions in thin films with strong surface anchoring and fixed thickness, analyzing their structure and interactions.
result: The stability and interaction of hopfions depend on the background phase, with certain configurations being more robust.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into controlling hopfions in confined systems, which could be relevant for future device applications.

title: Beyond The Arcsine Law: Aging Statistics Of The Occupation Time In Jump Processes
authors: Arthur Plaud And Olivier Bénichou
abstract:
Author(s): Arthur Plaud and Olivier Bénichou

Occupation times quantify how long a stochastic process remains in a region, and their single-time statistics are famously given by the arcsine law for Brownian and Lévy processes. By contrast, two-time occupation statistics—which directly probe temporal correlations and aging—have resisted exact ch…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014137] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies two-time occupation statistics in jump processes, revealing aging behavior beyond the classical arcsine law.
motivation: Occupation times are fundamental in stochastic processes, but two-time statistics and aging effects have not been fully characterized.
method: The authors derive exact expressions for two-time occupation probabilities in jump processes using renewal theory and asymptotic analysis.
result: They find that the joint distribution of occupation times exhibits aging, with correlations decaying as a power law, contrasting with the single-time arcsine law.
conclusion: The work provides a complete characterization of two-time occupation statistics, highlighting the importance of aging in stochastic processes.

title: Finite-size Scaling To Resolve Spurious Multifractality In The Two-dimensional Ising Model
authors: S. Jaroszewicz, N. Mendez, Maria P. Beccar-Varela, And Maria Cristina Mariani
abstract:
Author(s): S. Jaroszewicz, N. Mendez, Maria P. Beccar-Varela, and Maria Cristina Mariani

Multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis has emerged as a standard tool for characterizing scale invariance in complex systems, yet its application to discrete spin models is frequently marred by reports of “spurious multifractality” that contradict established theory. In this work, we resolve th…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014139] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper resolves spurious multifractality in the 2D Ising model using finite-size scaling.
motivation: Multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis often yields spurious multifractality in discrete spin models, contradicting theory.
method: The authors apply finite-size scaling to multifractal analysis of the 2D Ising model.
result: They show that apparent multifractality is a finite-size artifact and can be resolved by proper scaling.
conclusion: Finite-size scaling is essential to avoid misinterpretation of multifractality in spin systems.

title: Phenomenological Renormalization Group In Neuronal Models Near Criticality
authors: Kaio F. R. Nascimento, Daniel M. Castro, Gustavo G. Cambrainha, And Mauro Copelli
abstract:
Author(s): Kaio F. R. Nascimento, Daniel M. Castro, Gustavo G. Cambrainha, and Mauro Copelli

The phenomenological renormalization group (PRG) has been applied to the study of scale-invariant phenomena in neuronal data, providing evidence for critical phenomena in the brain. However, it remains unclear how reliably these observed signatures indicate genuine critical behavior, as it is not we…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014310] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies phenomenological renormalization group to neuronal models to test for criticality, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To determine whether scale-invariant signatures in neuronal data reliably indicate genuine critical behavior.
method: The authors apply the phenomenological renormalization group (PRG) to neuronal models and analyze the resulting scaling behavior.
result: The PRG method reveals signatures of criticality, but the reliability of these signatures as indicators of genuine critical behavior remains unclear.
conclusion: The study highlights the need for caution when interpreting scale-invariant phenomena in neuronal data as evidence of criticality.

title: Absence Of O(2) Symmetry In The Vicsek Model
authors: Yushin Takahashi, Kota Mitsui, Tsuyoshi Mizohata, And Hideyuki Miyahara
abstract:
Author(s): Yushin Takahashi, Kota Mitsui, Tsuyoshi Mizohata, and Hideyuki Miyahara

The phase transition in the Vicsek model is widely believed to be associated with spontaneous symmetry breaking of the two-dimensional rotational symmetry [MATH]. In this paper, we revisit the original model introduced by Vicsek et al. [
tldr: This paper demonstrates that the Vicsek model does not exhibit O(2) symmetry breaking, contrary to common belief.
motivation: The Vicsek model is a paradigmatic model for collective motion, and its phase transition is often attributed to spontaneous breaking of O(2) rotational symmetry. The authors aim to correct this misconception.
method: The authors revisit the original Vicsek model and analyze its symmetry properties using analytical arguments and numerical simulations.
result: They show that the model's dynamics and order parameter are not invariant under continuous rotations, thus O(2) symmetry is absent.
conclusion: The phase transition in the Vicsek model is not due to O(2) symmetry breaking, requiring a revised theoretical understanding.

title: First-passage Times For The Space-fractional Fokker-Planck Equation
authors: Christopher N. Angstmann, Daniel S. Han, Bruce I. Henry, And Boris Z. Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher N. Angstmann, Daniel S. Han, Bruce I. Henry, and Boris Z. Huang

We extend the random walk framework to include compounded steps, providing first-passage time (FPT) properties for a class of superdiffusive processes which are governed by the space-fractional spectral Fokker-Planck equation. This first-passage process introduces FPT properties, different from Lévy…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014136] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies first-passage times for superdiffusive processes governed by the space-fractional Fokker-Planck equation.
motivation: Understanding first-passage times in anomalous diffusion is important for various physical systems, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors extend the random walk framework to include compounded steps and derive first-passage time properties for space-fractional Fokker-Planck dynamics.
result: They obtain first-passage time distributions that differ from those of Lévy flights, highlighting the role of step correlations.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into first-passage phenomena in superdiffusive processes, but it is not relevant to the specified research directions.

title: Localization-delocalization Transition In Low-dimensional Asymmetric Resetting Random Walks
authors: Reza Sepehrinia
abstract:
Author(s): Reza Sepehrinia

We investigate biased random walks with stochastic resetting to previously visited sites and demonstrate how directional drift fundamentally alters the emergence of localized stationary states. We show that bias acts as a competing mechanism and can weaken or suppress localization. This competition …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014128] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies biased random walks with stochastic resetting, showing how directional drift affects localization-delocalization transitions.
motivation: To understand how bias competes with resetting in low-dimensional random walks, which is a classical stochastic process problem.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of biased random walks with resetting to previously visited sites.
result: Bias weakens or suppresses localization, leading to a localization-delocalization transition.
conclusion: The competition between drift and resetting fundamentally alters stationary state properties.

title: Continuous-time Random Walks With Asymmetric Waiting-time And Jump-length Distributions As A Model Of Biased Anomalous Transport
authors: Guohua Li, Andrey G. Cherstvy, Hong Zhang, Zeyu Tu, And Ralf Metzler
abstract:

Continuous-time random walks (CTRWs) are highly appreciated as a model of anomalous diffusion (AD) in complex media such as structured and heterogeneous environments. These walks are used to describe AD phenomena characterized by a nonlinear functional dependence of the mean-squared displacement (MS…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014129] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies continuous-time random walks with asymmetric waiting-time and jump-length distributions as a model of biased anomalous transport.
motivation: To understand anomalous diffusion in complex media, particularly when transport is biased due to asymmetric distributions.
method: The authors develop and analyze a CTRW model with coupled asymmetric waiting-time and jump-length distributions, deriving the mean-squared displacement and other transport properties.
result: The model captures biased anomalous transport, showing how asymmetry affects diffusion exponents and transport coefficients.
conclusion: Asymmetric CTRW models are useful for describing biased anomalous transport in heterogeneous environments.

title: Universality Of Order Statistics For Brownian Reshuffling
authors: Zdzislaw Burda, Mario Kieburg, And Tomasz Maciocha
abstract:
Author(s): Zdzislaw Burda, Mario Kieburg, and Tomasz Maciocha

In a one-dimensional gas of particles confined by an asymptotically power-law potential, the ordering of the particles changes as they perform Brownian motion. The authors show that the order statistics that describe how the particles are reshuffled are universal and independent of the potential’s exponent, while the timescale of the reshuffling does depend on it.

#UniversalBehavior #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014130] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the universality of order statistics in a one-dimensional gas of Brownian particles confined by a power-law potential.
motivation: Understanding how particle ordering changes over time in a confined gas is a fundamental statistical mechanics problem.
method: The authors analyze a one-dimensional gas with asymptotically power-law confining potential and derive order statistics for the reshuffling of particles due to Brownian motion.
result: The order statistics are universal and independent of the potential's exponent, while the reshuffling timescale depends on it.
conclusion: The universality of order statistics suggests a deeper underlying principle in stochastic many-body systems.

title: Dynamic Effects Of Electric Fields In A Hybrid-coupled Thermosensitive Neuronal Network
authors: Ediline L. F. Nguessap, Antonio C. Roque, And Fernando F. Ferreira
abstract:
Author(s): Ediline L. F. Nguessap, Antonio C. Roque, and Fernando F. Ferreira

The dynamics of thermosensitive FitzHugh-Nagumo neuronal networks under hybrid synaptic coupling and external electric fields is investigated in a ring topology. Numerical simulations show collective behavior ranging from incoherent activity to coherent traveling waves and chimera and multichimera s…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014218] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies collective dynamics in a thermosensitive neuronal network under electric fields, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding how electric fields affect neuronal network dynamics is important for neuroscience, but does not connect to the user's research interests.
method: Numerical simulations of a FitzHugh-Nagumo neuronal network with hybrid synaptic coupling and external electric fields in a ring topology.
result: Observed collective behaviors including incoherent activity, coherent traveling waves, and chimera states.
conclusion: The study provides insights into neuronal network dynamics but has no relevance to quantum information theory or quantum technologies.

title: Distance Function For Stochastic Matrices
authors: Antony R. Lee, Peter Tiňo, And Iain B. Styles
abstract:
Author(s): Antony R. Lee, Peter Tiňo, and Iain B. Styles

The ability to quantify the similarity of stochastic processes is important in a wide range of areas including communications, simulation, and operational research. Such processes are commonly modeled as Markov Chains and so a natural way to compare their similarity is to compute distances between p…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014125] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a distance function for stochastic matrices based on the Kullback-Leibler divergence rate, applied to Markov chains.
motivation: Quantifying similarity of stochastic processes is important in communications, simulation, and operational research.
method: The authors define a distance measure using the Kullback-Leibler divergence rate between Markov chains and prove its metric properties.
result: The distance function is shown to be a valid metric and is demonstrated on synthetic and real-world data.
conclusion: The proposed distance provides a principled way to compare stochastic processes modeled as Markov chains.

title: Intermediate Scattering Function Of Brownian Particles In A Tilted Cosine Potential
authors: Regina Rusch And Thomas Franosch
abstract:
Author(s): Regina Rusch and Thomas Franosch

We solve the Fokker-Planck equation for a Brownian particle in a tilted cosine potential and derive the intermediate scattering function (ISF), which captures the full spatiotemporal dynamics of the system. The model consists of a single overdamped Brownian particle in one dimension. We derive a gen…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014127] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper solves the Fokker-Planck equation for a Brownian particle in a tilted cosine potential and derives the intermediate scattering function.
motivation: Understanding the spatiotemporal dynamics of Brownian particles in periodic potentials is important for condensed matter physics and soft matter.
method: The authors solve the Fokker-Planck equation analytically and numerically to obtain the intermediate scattering function for an overdamped Brownian particle in a tilted cosine potential.
result: They derive a general expression for the ISF and analyze its dependence on tilt, potential strength, and wave vector.
conclusion: The work provides a complete characterization of the ISF for this model, which can be used to interpret scattering experiments.

title: Spin Glass Dynamics On Complex Hardware Topologies: A Bond-correlated Percolation Approach
authors: Viviana Gómez, Gabriel Téllez, And Fernando J. Gómez-Ruiz

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033099] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin glass dynamics on complex hardware topologies using a bond-correlated percolation approach.
motivation: Understanding how frustration and disorder shape relaxation in complex systems is central to statistical physics and quantum annealing.
method: The authors develop a bond-correlated percolation model to analyze spin glass dynamics on complex hardware topologies.
result: The approach provides insights into relaxation processes in spin glasses on non-trivial network structures.
conclusion: The work contributes to statistical physics but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Nonperturbative Effects Of Short-range Spatial Correlations At The Two-particle Level
authors: Michael Meixner, Matthias Reitner, Thomas Schäfer, And Alessandro Toschi
