[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033093] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonperturbative effects of short-range spatial correlations in two-dimensional systems using cellular dynamical mean-field theory, focusing on the Mott transition.
motivation: To understand how short-range correlations drive the breakdown of self-consistent perturbation theory and the associated Mott transition in two-dimensional systems.
method: Cellular dynamical mean-field theory (CDMFT) is employed to analyze short-range correlations and their nonperturbative effects.
result: The study identifies the breakdown of perturbation theory due to short-range correlations and characterizes the CDMFT Mott transition.
conclusion: Short-range spatial correlations play a crucial role in nonperturbative physics of correlated electron systems, with implications for understanding Mott transitions.

title: Twist-driven Interlayer Hybridization And Multiple Mobility Edges In Bilayer Quasiperiodic Lattices
authors: Ankit Mishra And Kang Hao Cheong
abstract:
Author(s): Ankit Mishra and Kang Hao Cheong

We investigate two coupled one-dimensional Aubry-André-Harper rings with [MATH] sites, where a site-dependent angular twist in the second ring generates a spatially varying mosaic of distance-modulated couplings. By varying the quasiperiodic potential strength [MATH] and twist periodicity [MATH], we find mul…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033079] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies mobility edges in bilayer quasiperiodic lattices with twist-induced interlayer hybridization.
motivation: Understanding localization and mobility edges in quasiperiodic systems is a fundamental problem in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors analyze two coupled Aubry-André-Harper rings with a site-dependent angular twist, varying quasiperiodic potential strength and twist periodicity.
result: They find multiple mobility edges and rich phase diagrams due to the interplay of quasiperiodicity and interlayer coupling.
conclusion: The work reveals new phenomena in quasiperiodic systems but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Characterizing Topology At Nonzero Temperature: Topological Invariants And Indicators In The Extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Model
authors: Julia D. Hannukainen And Nigel R. Cooper
abstract:
Author(s): Julia D. Hannukainen and Nigel R. Cooper

We compare three complementary diagnostics for mixed Gaussian states at nonzero temperature, focusing on the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain and its inversion-symmetric extension. While the ensemble geometric phase, a mixed-state generalization of the Zak phase, remains well defined at nonzero temp…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033080] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes topological invariants for mixed Gaussian states at nonzero temperature in the extended SSH model.
motivation: Understanding topology at finite temperature is important for realistic systems, but the paper focuses on condensed matter topology rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors compare three diagnostics: ensemble geometric phase, Uhlmann phase, and a many-body invariant, applied to the SSH chain and its inversion-symmetric extension.
result: The ensemble geometric phase remains well-defined at nonzero temperature and captures topological transitions, while the other diagnostics show limitations.
conclusion: The ensemble geometric phase is a useful indicator of topology at finite temperature, but the work is primarily a condensed matter study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Combinatorial Reasoning For Large Language Models
authors: Carlos Flores-Garrigós, Gaurav Dev, Michael Falkenthal, Alejandro Gomez Cadavid, Anton Simen, Shubham Kumar, Enrique Solano, And Narendra N. Hegade
abstract:
Author(s): Carlos Flores-Garrigós, Gaurav Dev, Michael Falkenthal, Alejandro Gomez Cadavid, Anton Simen, Shubham Kumar, Enrique Solano, and Narendra N. Hegade

We design and implement a quantum combinatorial reasoning framework for large language models (QCR-LLM), integrating a real quantum computer in the hybrid workflow. QCR-LLM reformulates reasoning aggregation as a higher-order unconstrained binary optimization problem. In this sense, reasoning fragme…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033070] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum combinatorial reasoning framework for large language models, integrating a real quantum computer to reformulate reasoning aggregation as a higher-order unconstrained binary optimization problem.
motivation: Large language models often struggle with complex reasoning tasks; quantum computing may offer advantages in combinatorial optimization for reasoning aggregation.
method: The authors design a hybrid workflow where reasoning fragments are encoded into a higher-order unconstrained binary optimization problem and solved using a quantum computer.
result: The framework demonstrates improved reasoning accuracy on benchmark tasks compared to classical baselines, leveraging quantum optimization.
conclusion: Quantum combinatorial reasoning can enhance LLM performance, suggesting a promising direction for hybrid quantum-classical AI systems.

title: Detection Time Distribution Predicted Using Absorbing Boundary Conditions And Imaginary Potentials
authors: Alireza Jozani And Roderich Tumulka
abstract:
Author(s): Alireza Jozani and Roderich Tumulka

There are several inequivalent proposals in the literature for how to compute the probability distribution of the time that a detector registers for the arrival of a quantum particle. For three of these proposals, based on two kinds of absorbing boundary conditions and imaginary potentials, we compu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033072] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper computes probability distributions of detection times for quantum particles using absorbing boundary conditions and imaginary potentials.
motivation: There are multiple inequivalent proposals for computing arrival time distributions in quantum mechanics, and the authors aim to compare them.
method: The authors compute detection time distributions for three proposals: two kinds of absorbing boundary conditions and imaginary potentials.
result: The distributions from the three proposals are compared, showing differences and similarities.
conclusion: The work provides a comparative analysis of detection time distributions, but does not resolve which proposal is correct.

title: Quantum Solver For Single-impurity Anderson Models With Particle-hole Symmetry
authors: M. Karabin, T. Sohail, D. Bykov, E. A. Coello Pérez, S. Ghosh, M. Gopalakrishnan Meena, S. Kim, A. Shehata, I.-S. Suh, H. Terletska, And M. Eisenbach
abstract:
Author(s): M. Karabin, T. Sohail, D. Bykov, E. A. Coello Pérez, S. Ghosh, M. Gopalakrishnan Meena, S. Kim, A. Shehata, I.-S. Suh, H. Terletska, and M. Eisenbach

Quantum embedding methods, such as dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT), provide a powerful framework for investigating strongly correlated materials. A central computational bottleneck in DMFT is in solving the Anderson impurity model (AIM), whose exact solution is classically intractable for large b…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033066] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a quantum algorithm for solving the single-impurity Anderson model with particle-hole symmetry, targeting a computational bottleneck in dynamical mean-field theory.
motivation: Solving the Anderson impurity model is classically intractable for large systems, and quantum computers may offer a speedup for this task in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors design a quantum solver that exploits particle-hole symmetry to reduce resource requirements, and implement it on a quantum simulator or hardware.
result: The quantum solver achieves accurate results for small system sizes, demonstrating feasibility but not yet outperforming classical methods.
conclusion: Quantum algorithms can potentially accelerate DMFT calculations, but practical advantage requires further error mitigation and larger quantum devices.

title: Interaction-Driven Topological Transitions In Monolayer ${\mathrm{TaIrTe}}_{4}$
authors: Jiangxu Li, Jian Tang, Cheng Xu, Louis Primeau, Thomas Siyuan Ding, Rahul Soni, Tiema Qian, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ni Ni, Adrian Del Maestro, Qiong Ma, And Yang Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Jiangxu Li, Jian Tang, Cheng Xu, Louis Primeau, Thomas Siyuan Ding, Rahul Soni, Tiema Qian, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ni Ni, Adrian Del Maestro, Qiong Ma, and Yang Zhang

Theoretical and experimental mapping of monolayer TaIrTe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031017] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies interaction-driven topological phase transitions in monolayer TaIrTe4 without moiré engineering.
motivation: To explore topological phases in a single naturally layered crystal and understand the role of electron interactions.
method: Combines theoretical modeling (likely DFT or tight-binding) with experimental measurements (transport, STM, etc.) on monolayer TaIrTe4.
result: Reveals a rich landscape of interaction-driven topological phases in the material.
conclusion: Monolayer TaIrTe4 is a promising platform for studying topological phases without the need for moiré superlattices.

title: Limits Of Inference In Complex Systems: When Stochastic Models Become Indistinguishable
authors: Javier Aguilar, Miguel A. Muñoz, And Sandro Azaele
abstract:
Author(s): Javier Aguilar, Miguel A. Muñoz, and Sandro Azaele

A path-inference framework quantifies data resolution limits that render distinct stochastic models empirically indistinguishable and offers guidelines for designing experimental measurements that maximize information extraction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031015] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a path-inference framework to quantify when distinct stochastic models become empirically indistinguishable due to finite data resolution.
motivation: In complex systems, multiple stochastic models may fit the same data, making it difficult to infer the true underlying dynamics. The authors aim to formalize the limits of model distinguishability.
method: They propose a path-inference framework based on information theory, analyzing how data resolution and sample size affect the ability to discriminate between different stochastic processes.
result: The framework provides quantitative bounds on the resolution required to distinguish models, showing that many models become indistinguishable under realistic experimental conditions.
conclusion: The results offer guidelines for designing experiments that maximize information extraction and highlight fundamental limits in model inference for complex systems.

title: Statistical Physics Of Deep Learning: Optimal Learning Of A Multilayer Perceptron Near Interpolation
authors: Jean Barbier, Francesco Camilli, Minh-Toan Nguyen, Mauro Pastore, And Rudy Skerk
abstract:
Author(s): Jean Barbier, Francesco Camilli, Minh-Toan Nguyen, Mauro Pastore, and Rudy Skerk

Using statistical physics and random matrix theory, researchers derive the generalization error of a deep fully connected neural network and uncover the mechanisms governing its behavior as feature learning progressively propagates across layers.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031014] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses statistical physics and random matrix theory to analyze generalization error in deep neural networks near interpolation.
motivation: Understanding generalization in deep learning is a central challenge; the authors aim to derive exact generalization error for a multilayer perceptron.
method: They apply tools from statistical physics (replica method, cavity method) and random matrix theory to a deep fully connected neural network model.
result: They derive the generalization error and uncover how feature learning propagates across layers, revealing mechanisms governing network behavior near interpolation.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for deep learning generalization using physics-inspired methods, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Identifying Geometric Third-Order Nonlinear Transport In Disordered Materials
authors: Zhen-Hao Gong, Zhi-Hao Wei, Hai-Zhou Lu, And X. C. Xie
abstract:
Author(s): Zhen-Hao Gong, Zhi-Hao Wei, Hai-Zhou Lu, and X. C. Xie

A theoretical data-analysis tool resolves the chaotic interpretation of nonlinear electronic transport data, providing a structured method to extract quantum geometric properties from realistic materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031012] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a data-analysis tool to extract geometric third-order nonlinear transport properties from disordered materials.
motivation: Nonlinear electronic transport data in disordered materials is often chaotic and difficult to interpret; a structured method is needed to extract quantum geometric properties.
method: The authors propose a theoretical data-analysis tool that systematically resolves the chaotic interpretation of nonlinear transport data.
result: The tool provides a structured way to identify geometric third-order nonlinear transport signatures from realistic material data.
conclusion: The method enables reliable extraction of quantum geometric properties from nonlinear transport experiments in disordered systems.

title: Floquet-Based Ising Machines Escape Local Minima In Qubo Problems
authors: Nicolas Casilli, Seunghwi Kim, Sunil Mittal, Marvin Onabajo, Andrea Alù, And Cristian Cassella
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Casilli, Seunghwi Kim, Sunil Mittal, Marvin Onabajo, Andrea Alù, and Cristian Cassella

The analog Floquet solver incorporates Floquet amplitude modulations to help it escape local minima, significantly improving the accuracy of parametric oscillator-based Ising machines in solving optimization problems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031010] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a Floquet-based Ising machine that uses amplitude modulations to escape local minima in QUBO problems.
motivation: Parametric oscillator-based Ising machines often get stuck in local minima when solving optimization problems; the authors aim to improve solution accuracy.
method: They incorporate Floquet amplitude modulations into the analog solver to help the system escape local minima.
result: The Floquet-based approach significantly improves the accuracy of solving QUBO problems compared to standard parametric oscillator Ising machines.
conclusion: Floquet amplitude modulations are an effective technique to enhance the performance of Ising machines for combinatorial optimization.

title: Candidate For A Fractional Topological Insulator In Twisted ${\mathrm{MoTe}}_{2}$
authors: Yiping Wang, Gillian E. Minarik, Weijie Li, Yves Kwan, Shuai Yuan, Eric Anderson, Chaowei Hu, Julian Ingham, Jeongheon Choe, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Xavier Roy, Jiun-Haw Chu, Raquel Queiroz, James C. Hone, N. Regnault, Xiaodong Xu, And Xiaoyang Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Yiping Wang, Gillian E. Minarik, Weijie Li, Yves Kwan, Shuai Yuan, Eric Anderson, Chaowei Hu, Julian Ingham, Jeongheon Choe, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Xavier Roy, Jiun-Haw Chu, Raquel Queiroz, James C. Hone, N. Regnault, Xiaodong Xu, and Xiaoyang Zhu

Pump-probe modulation spectroscopy of a MoTe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031009] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental signatures of a fractional topological insulator in twisted MoTe2 bilayers.
motivation: Fractional topological insulators are a predicted phase of matter combining topology and strong correlations, but experimental evidence has been lacking.
method: Pump-probe modulation spectroscopy was used to measure the out-of-plane antiferromagnetic response in a MoTe2 bilayer superlattice.
result: The observed antiferromagnetic response provides experimental signatures consistent with a putative fractional topological insulator state.
conclusion: The findings suggest twisted MoTe2 is a promising platform for realizing fractional topological insulators.

title: Covariant Path Integrals For Quantum Fields Backreacting On Classical Space-Time
authors: Jonathan Oppenheim And Zachary Weller-Davies
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Oppenheim and Zachary Weller-Davies

Researchers have developed a mathematical framework to bridge the gap between Einstein’s classical gravity and quantum mechanics. Their theory allows matter to remain quantum while space-time stays classical, offering a way to test if space and time truly require a quantum explanation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031007] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a covariant path integral framework for quantum fields on a classical spacetime, aiming to reconcile quantum mechanics with classical gravity.
motivation: To bridge the gap between quantum field theory and general relativity by allowing matter to be quantum while spacetime remains classical, providing a testable framework for quantum gravity.
method: The authors construct a covariant path integral formalism that couples quantum fields to a classical spacetime background, incorporating backreaction effects.
result: They derive a consistent mathematical framework that describes the dynamics of quantum fields on a classical spacetime, including the backreaction of quantum fields on the classical geometry.
conclusion: The framework offers a potential avenue for testing whether spacetime is fundamentally classical or quantum, and provides a tool for studying semiclassical gravity.

title: Electric-Field Control Of Interlayer Binding And Friction In $h$-BN Contacts
authors: Penghua Ying, Michael Urbakh, And Oded Hod
abstract:
Author(s): Penghua Ying, Michael Urbakh, and Oded Hod

External electric fields can be used to control sliding resistance in layered materials, providing a way to control friction in some systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031003] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electric-field control of interlayer binding and friction in h-BN contacts, a topic in nanoscale tribology.
motivation: Understanding and controlling friction at the nanoscale is important for applications in micro- and nano-electromechanical systems.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations and classical molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the effect of external electric fields on interlayer binding and sliding friction in hexagonal boron nitride contacts.
result: They find that electric fields can significantly modulate interlayer binding energies and friction forces, enabling control of sliding resistance.
conclusion: External electric fields provide a viable route to actively control friction in layered materials like h-BN.

title: Agentic Exploration Of Physics Models
authors: Maximilian Nägele And Florian Marquardt
abstract:
Author(s): Maximilian Nägele and Florian Marquardt

ꜱᴄɪᴇxᴘʟᴏʀᴇʀ, a generalist artificial scientist agent based on a large-language model, automates the process of scientific research and discovery and uncovers underlying models of diverse physical systems without task-specific fine-tuning.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031002] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an AI agent that automates scientific discovery in physics by exploring and modeling physical systems without task-specific fine-tuning.
motivation: To accelerate scientific discovery by automating the process of hypothesis generation and model building in physics.
method: The authors develop SciExplorer, a large-language-model-based agent that iteratively proposes experiments, analyzes data, and refines models of physical systems.
result: The agent successfully uncovers underlying models for diverse physical systems, demonstrating generalist scientific discovery capabilities.
conclusion: LLM-based agents can automate parts of the scientific research process, potentially speeding up discovery in physics.

title: Rare Cage Escapes Drive Relaxation In Deeply Supercooled Liquids
authors: Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, And Walter Kob
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, and Walter Kob

Simulations conducted significantly below the mode coupling temperature allow dynamic properties of glass forming systems to be uncovered.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021061] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Simulations of deeply supercooled liquids reveal that rare cage escapes drive relaxation dynamics.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic mechanisms of relaxation in supercooled liquids is crucial for glass transition theory.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations are performed at temperatures significantly below the mode coupling temperature to analyze particle motion.
result: Relaxation is governed by rare events where particles escape from their local cages, leading to cooperative rearrangements.
conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of rare events in glassy dynamics and provide insight into the nature of the glass transition.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes, bridging the gap between theory and experimental demonstrations.
motivation: Previous complexity-theoretic results for BosonSampling applied only to the dilute regime, while experiments operate in the saturated regime; this work provides the theoretical underpinnings for those experiments.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of BosonSampling when the number of modes scales linearly with the number of photons, using techniques from computational complexity theory and quantum optics.
result: They show that BosonSampling in the saturated regime remains hard for classical computers under plausible conjectures, and they provide evidence for the hardness.
conclusion: The results justify the use of BosonSampling as a candidate for demonstrating quantum advantage in current photonic experiments.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, and Cristian D. Batista

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum chiral solitons in spin chains and their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, detectable via neutron scattering.
motivation: To develop a nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons and understand their role as low-energy excitations in ferromagnetic spin chains.
method: A nonperturbative quantization approach is applied to chiral solitons in spin chains, analyzing their dynamics and condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid.
result: Chiral solitons condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase, detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.
conclusion: The framework provides a way to observe chiral solitons experimentally and advances understanding of soliton dynamics in quantum spin systems.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To understand non-perturbative aspects of conformal field theories, particularly fermionic ones, using a novel noncommutative geometry approach.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative discretization of the sphere, to simulate fermionic CFTs and analyze their spectra and operator content.
result: They find evidence for emergent supersymmetry in the interacting fermionic CFTs on the fuzzy sphere.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere provides a powerful tool for studying strongly coupled CFTs, and emergent supersymmetry may be a generic feature of such systems.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies topological Dirac magnons in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature, focusing on the stability of magnon gaps near the Curie point.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of topological magnon gaps at finite temperatures is crucial for designing spintronic devices, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling of magnon interactions to simulate the behavior of topological magnon gaps as temperature approaches the Curie point.
result: They find that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable even near the Curie temperature.
conclusion: The results provide a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices based on topological magnons.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network, showing that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions.
motivation: To explore whether neural networks can serve as collision-resistant hash functions for cryptographic protocols.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network using theoretical and algorithmic approaches.
result: Efficient algorithms are shown to fail in finding collisions, suggesting that such neural networks may be collision resistant.
conclusion: The findings are relevant for defining new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: To develop a general method for predicting physical links in networks without requiring detailed knowledge of the dynamics.
method: The authors propose a framework that leverages physical principles to infer causal relationships from observed network dynamics.
result: The framework is demonstrated to accurately predict links across a variety of networked systems.
conclusion: The approach provides a physics-based tool for network inference with broad applicability.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies anyon superfluidity of excitons in quantum Hall bilayers, focusing on topological criticality and exotic collective quantum states.
motivation: To understand and engineer exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall bilayers via topological criticality.
method: Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers, likely using field theory or numerical methods.
result: Topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids.
conclusion: This provides a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications
authors: Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. Mcclean, Thomas O’brien, And Nicholas C. Rubin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. McClean, Thomas O’Brien, and Nicholas C. Rubin

A proposed five-stage framework outlines the path to useful quantum computing, detailing the scientific milestones required to bridge the gap between theory and real-world utility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, outlining scientific milestones.
motivation: To bridge the gap between theoretical quantum computing and real-world utility by defining clear stages of progress.
method: The authors propose a structured framework with five stages, each with specific milestones, based on their expertise in quantum algorithms and hardware.
result: A five-stage roadmap is presented, but no new technical results or experiments are reported.
conclusion: The framework provides a high-level guide for the field but does not contain novel technical contributions.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a complete quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, demonstrating its use as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a powerful invariant in knot theory with applications in topology and quantum gravity, but its approximation is classically hard, motivating a quantum algorithm.
method: The authors design an end-to-end quantum algorithm that maps the Jones polynomial to a quantum circuit, using techniques from topological quantum computing and implementing it on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: They experimentally compute the Jones polynomial for several knots on a trapped-ion quantum computer, showing agreement with theoretical predictions and highlighting the potential for quantum advantage.
conclusion: The work establishes a practical benchmark for quantum computers and suggests that quantum algorithms for the Jones polynomial may offer advantages over classical methods.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, covering HHL and post-HHL developments.
motivation: Quantum linear system solvers are a key subroutine in many quantum algorithms, and a structured review is needed to organize the rapidly growing literature.
method: The paper systematically reviews algorithmic techniques including HHL, variable-time amplitude amplification, adiabatic approaches, and block-encoding methods, with complexity analysis and application examples.
result: It provides a taxonomy of QLSP algorithms, compares their query complexities, and discusses applications in machine learning, differential equations, and quantum chemistry.
conclusion: Quantum linear system solvers have matured significantly, but practical implementation remains challenging due to resource requirements; future work should focus on near-term implementations and error mitigation.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism, which has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes experimental and theoretical results on 2D van der Waals magnets, including topics like topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, and spintronics.
result: The review highlights the rapid progress in understanding magnetic phenomena in 2D materials and their potential for applications.
conclusion: The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from frustrated lattice geometry.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, analyzing electronic structure and many-body effects.
result: Identifies key phenomena including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, and sublattice interference effects leading to superconductivity and orbital magnetism.
conclusion: Kagome metals provide a rich platform for studying correlated electron physics and topological states, with potential for new quantum phases.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: To provide an updated overview of spin-glass research and highlight the synergy between experimental, theoretical, and computational approaches.
method: Review of experimental techniques, theoretical models, and large-scale simulations of spin glasses.
result: Summarizes key advances in understanding spin-glass dynamics and identifies future research opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich field with broad applications, and continued interdisciplinary collaboration is essential.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a paradigmatic example of frustrated magnetism.
method: Review of literature on Kitaev models, material candidates, and experimental probes such as neutron scattering and thermal transport.
result: Summarizes key candidate materials and their topological properties, including chiral edge modes.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids remain an active area of research with potential connections to quantum computation, but the review does not present new results.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for spintronic devices, but their quantum aspects are less explored; this review aims to bridge that gap.
method: The paper surveys theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion formation, quantum interactions, and quantum features of skyrmions themselves.
result: It highlights quantum-mechanical effects in skyrmion dynamics and interactions, and discusses potential quantum functionalities.
conclusion: Quantum properties of skyrmions may enable new applications in quantum information and spintronics, but the field is still nascent.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations through violated assumptions.
motivation: To clarify why certain measurements exceed classical thermodynamic bounds and to guide the design of materials with extreme properties.
method: The paper surveys a wide range of examples from different fields, analyzing which underlying assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linear response) are violated in each case.
result: It identifies that apparent violations arise from non-equilibrium conditions, nonlinear effects, or structural hierarchy, and shows how these can be exploited to create materials with properties beyond classical limits.
conclusion: Classical thermodynamic bounds are not fundamental limits but rather constraints under specific assumptions; violating those assumptions allows materials to exceed the bounds, enabling novel material design.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on implementing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems for quantum many-body physics.
motivation: To explore exotic geometries beyond standard lattices for simulating phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: Reviews experimental and theoretical approaches for realizing synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries using atomic, photonic, and electronic platforms.
result: Summarizes progress in creating fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher-dimensional systems, enabling new quantum simulations.
conclusion: These synthetic geometries open avenues for studying quantum many-body physics in regimes previously inaccessible, with connections to topology and fundamental physics.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in polar active matter, covering single-particle and collective behaviors.
motivation: To unify the understanding of self-alignment in active systems and highlight its potential for biology, smart materials, and robotics.
method: Review of existing models and experimental systems, presenting a unified mathematical and conceptual framework.
result: Self-alignment enables novel behaviors such as orbiting in harmonic traps and synchronized motion in dense assemblies.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a fundamental property that reshapes motion in active systems, with broad implications for applications.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical and experimental efforts to study gravity's effects on massive quantum systems, focusing on decoherence, collapse, and entanglement mediated by gravity.
motivation: Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force, and massive quantum systems may serve as probes to test quantum aspects of gravity.
method: The paper reviews theories of gravity-induced decoherence and collapse, and describes experimental setups using matter-wave interferometry and optomechanics to test these effects.
result: The review summarizes current theoretical models and experimental progress, noting that experiments testing gravity-mediated entanglement are underway.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems can provide insights into the interplay between quantum mechanics and gravity, guiding future theoretical and experimental work.

title: Valley-Engineered Landau Polaritons In A Van Der Waals Semiconductor Microcavity
authors: Xinyue Zhang, Hongming Zhang, Yaofeng Zhu, Hang Zhou, Song Luo, Long Xu, Xin Li, Yuquan Zhou, Yan Liu, Zheng Lv, Yuxin Duan, Zhao Xu, Haodong Cheng, Long Zhang, And Zhanghai Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyue Zhang, Hongming Zhang, Yaofeng Zhu, Hang Zhou, Song Luo, Long Xu, Xin Li, Yuquan Zhou, Yan Liu, Zheng Lv, Yuxin Duan, Zhao Xu, Haodong Cheng, Long Zhang, and Zhanghai Chen

Integrating a WSe
[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046904] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates valley-engineered Landau polaritons in a WSe2 monolayer embedded in an optical microcavity, enabling light-mediated valley control of quantum many-body states.
motivation: To achieve valley control of quantum many-body states using light-matter coupling in a van der Waals semiconductor microcavity.
method: A WSe2 monolayer is integrated into an optical microcavity, and Landau polaritons are generated under magnetic fields, with valley polarization controlled by circularly polarized light.
result: Valley-engineered Landau polaritons are observed, demonstrating light-mediated valley control.
conclusion: The work provides a platform for valleytronics and quantum control in two-dimensional semiconductors.

title: Polaron-Driven Switching Of Octupolar Order In Doped $5{\mathrm{d}}^{2}$ Double Perovskite
authors: Dario Fiore Mosca, Lorenzo Celiberti, Leonid V. Pourovskii, And Cesare Franchini
abstract:
Author(s): Dario Fiore Mosca, Lorenzo Celiberti, Leonid V. Pourovskii, and Cesare Franchini

We investigate how doping-induced small polarons impact the low-temperature multipolar orders of the [MATH] double perovskite [MATH]. By computing intersite exchange interactions between [MATH] localized hole polarons and [MATH] magnetic ions from first p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046504] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies polaron-driven switching of octupolar order in a doped double perovskite, focusing on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how doping-induced small polarons affect low-temperature multipolar orders in 5d^2 double perovskites.
method: First-principles calculations of intersite exchange interactions between localized hole polarons and magnetic ions.
result: Polarons can switch the octupolar order, revealing a mechanism for controlling multipolar phases.
conclusion: The findings highlight the role of polarons in tuning electronic orders, relevant for materials design but not for quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Imprints Of Asymptotic Freedom On Confining Strings
authors: Jan Albert And Alexandre Homrich
abstract:
Author(s): Jan Albert and Alexandre Homrich

We consider the Polyakov loop correlator in the confining phase of large [MATH] Yang-Mills theory in three and four dimensions. It can be computed by summing over the exchange of closed flux tubes winding around the thermal cycle. At short separations, the leading divergence is controlled by perturbati…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 041601] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Polyakov loop correlator in large N Yang-Mills theory, focusing on the imprint of asymptotic freedom on confining strings.
motivation: Understanding the short-distance behavior of confining strings in non-Abelian gauge theories is important for connecting perturbative and non-perturbative aspects of QCD.
method: The authors compute the Polyakov loop correlator in the confining phase using a sum over closed flux tubes, and analyze the leading divergence at short separations via perturbative methods.
result: They find that the leading divergence is controlled by perturbative asymptotic freedom, providing a connection between the string tension and the running coupling.
conclusion: The results show that asymptotic freedom leaves clear imprints on the properties of confining strings, bridging perturbative and non-perturbative regimes.

title: Integrated Soliton Microcombs Beyond The Turnkey Limit
authors: Ze Wang, Tianyu Xu, Yuanlei Wang, Kaixuan Zhu, Xinrui Luo, Haoyang Luo, Junqi Wang, Bo Ni, Yiwen Yang, Qihuang Gong, Yun-Feng Xiao, Bei-Bei Li, And Qi-Fan Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Ze Wang, Tianyu Xu, Yuanlei Wang, Kaixuan Zhu, Xinrui Luo, Haoyang Luo, Junqi Wang, Bo Ni, Yiwen Yang, Qihuang Gong, Yun-Feng Xiao, Bei-Bei Li, and Qi-Fan Yang

Self-injection locking enables integrated soliton microcombs with turnkey initiation and improved coherence, but it also pins the pump close to resonance, limiting the access to large detuning for broader combs. Here, we use an auxiliary resonator to dynamically hybridize the pump mode, enabling adi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 043802] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates an integrated soliton microcomb platform that uses an auxiliary resonator to achieve broad comb spectra beyond the turnkey limit.
motivation: Integrated soliton microcombs are important for applications like spectroscopy and telecommunications, but turnkey self-injection locking limits the achievable comb bandwidth. The authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: They employ an auxiliary resonator to dynamically hybridize the pump mode, enabling adiabatic access to large pump detunings and thus broader soliton microcombs.
result: The hybridized pump mode allows generation of soliton microcombs with significantly broader spectra than conventional turnkey schemes.
conclusion: This approach extends the capabilities of integrated soliton microcombs, making them more versatile for practical applications.

title: Nmr Evidence For Spontaneous Electronic Chiral Order In URhSn
authors: Y. Tokunaga, T. Ishitobi, H. Sakai, S. Kambe, H. Harima, A. Nakamura, A. Maurya, D. Li, Y. Homma, F. Honda, D. Aoki, And Y. Shimizu
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Tokunaga, T. Ishitobi, H. Sakai, S. Kambe, H. Harima, A. Nakamura, A. Maurya, D. Li, Y. Homma, F. Honda, D. Aoki, and Y. Shimizu

The first direct evidence of spontaneous electronic chiral order in URhSn, a strongly correlated material without an inherently chiral lattice structure, fundamentally challenges the prevailing notion that electronic chirality requires a chiral crystal framework.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046501] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports NMR evidence for spontaneous electronic chiral order in URhSn, a strongly correlated material without a chiral lattice.
motivation: To challenge the prevailing notion that electronic chirality requires a chiral crystal framework by finding direct evidence in a non-chiral lattice.
method: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) measurements on URhSn single crystals to detect chiral order.
result: Observation of spontaneous electronic chiral order in URhSn, providing the first direct evidence of such order in a material without an inherently chiral lattice.
conclusion: Electronic chirality can emerge in non-chiral lattices, fundamentally changing the understanding of chiral order in strongly correlated materials.

title: Orbital-spin Conversion In Solid High-order Harmonic Generation By Ring Configurations
authors: Sheng Luo, Xiaoqi Fei, Zixi Guo, Yang Li, Shiqi Liang, Xiaosong Zhu, And Jianghua Luo
abstract:
Author(s): Sheng Luo, Xiaoqi Fei, Zixi Guo, Yang Li, Shiqi Liang, Xiaosong Zhu, and Jianghua Luo

We theoretically investigate the interaction between azimuthal vector vortex beams and a segmented ring medium, revealing orbital-to-spin conversion in strong-field high-order harmonic generation. We show that engineered gaps in the ring target break the light-matter symmetry and mediate the transfe…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013122] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies orbital-to-spin conversion in high-order harmonic generation using vector vortex beams and segmented ring targets.
motivation: To understand and control the transfer of orbital angular momentum to spin angular momentum in strong-field light-matter interactions.
method: Theoretical investigation using azimuthal vector vortex beams interacting with a segmented ring medium, with engineered gaps to break symmetry.
result: Orbital-to-spin conversion is observed in high-order harmonic generation, mediated by the broken symmetry from the gaps.
conclusion: The work reveals a new mechanism for angular momentum conversion in nonlinear optics, with potential applications in ultrafast optics and light-matter control.

title: Origins Of The Intrinsic Noise Of Zero-field Metastable Helium-4 Optically Pumped Magnetometers
authors: Alexandre Stathopulos, Rudy Romain, Sergey Mitryukovskiy, And Agustin Palacios-Laloy
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Stathopulos, Rudy Romain, Sergey Mitryukovskiy, and Agustin Palacios-Laloy

We report a comprehensive characterization of the intrinsic noise of a single-beam [MATH]-based vector optically pumped magnetometer, and identify its main origins. In its optimal regime, the sensor provided vector magnetic readings with noise below $30{0ex}}\mathrm{…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012619] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the intrinsic noise of a zero-field metastable helium-4 optically pumped magnetometer.
motivation: Understanding the origins of noise in optically pumped magnetometers is important for improving their sensitivity and performance.
method: The authors perform a comprehensive experimental characterization of the intrinsic noise of a single-beam vector magnetometer, identifying main noise sources.
result: In its optimal regime, the sensor provides vector magnetic readings with noise below 300 fT/√Hz.
conclusion: The identified noise sources can guide future improvements in magnetometer design.

title: Calculating Resonance Using Parametric Equations Of Motion In The Limit Of The Complex Absorbing Potential Strength Parameter ($η→{0}^{+}$)
authors: Deepak Kumar And Ashish Kumar Gupta
abstract:
Author(s): Deepak Kumar and Ashish Kumar Gupta

Since complex absorbing potentials (CAPs) are nonphysical in nature, they can introduce artificial perturbations into the system, which may lead to shifts in the calculated energy. This study presents a methodology to eliminate artificial reflections caused by the CAP using a backward parametric equ…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012818] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to eliminate artificial reflections from complex absorbing potentials in resonance calculations using parametric equations of motion.
motivation: Complex absorbing potentials introduce artificial perturbations that shift calculated energies; the authors aim to correct these shifts.
method: A backward parametric equation of motion is derived in the limit of the CAP strength parameter approaching zero to remove artificial reflections.
result: The methodology successfully eliminates artificial reflections, yielding more accurate resonance energies.
conclusion: The proposed parametric approach improves the accuracy of resonance calculations by mitigating CAP-induced artifacts.

title: Isotope Shifts In Heliumlike Carbon: Probes Of Nuclear Structure And New Bosons
authors: Xiao-Qiu Qi, Fang-Fei Wu, Zong-Chao Yan, Zhen-Xiang Zhong, Li-Yan Tang, Ai-Xi Chen, And Ting-Yun Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Xiao-Qiu Qi, Fang-Fei Wu, Zong-Chao Yan, Zhen-Xiang Zhong, Li-Yan Tang, Ai-Xi Chen, and Ting-Yun Shi

We present high-precision calculations of isotope shifts for the [MATH] and [MATH] transitions in heliumlike [MATH], with mass-shift u…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012817] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: High-precision calculations of isotope shifts in heliumlike carbon to probe nuclear structure and search for new bosons.
motivation: Isotope shifts provide a sensitive probe of nuclear properties and can constrain new physics beyond the Standard Model.
method: Variational calculations with explicitly correlated basis functions and relativistic corrections are used to compute transition energies and isotope shifts.
result: Accurate isotope shift predictions are obtained for the 1s2p 1P1 → 1s2s 1S0 and 1s2p 3P2 → 1s2s 3S1 transitions in C4+.
conclusion: The results enable experimental tests of nuclear structure models and searches for new bosons via King plot analysis.

title: Wetting Of Quantum Fluids: A Route To Free-standing Shell-shaped Quantum Droplets
authors: Francesco Ancilotto
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Ancilotto

We investigate wetting phenomena between self-bound quantum fluids in a three-component Bose mixture of [MATH], and [MATH] atoms. Within a density-functional approach including mean-field interactions and Lee-Huang-Yang quantum-fluctuation corrections, we cons…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013317] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wetting phenomena in quantum fluid droplets using density-functional theory, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand wetting behavior of self-bound quantum fluids in a three-component Bose mixture.
method: Density-functional approach including mean-field interactions and Lee-Huang-Yang quantum-fluctuation corrections.
result: Predicts conditions for wetting and formation of free-standing shell-shaped quantum droplets.
conclusion: The work provides insights into quantum fluid wetting but does not address information or thermodynamic aspects.

title: Singularly Isostatic And Geometrically Unstable Rigidity Of Metal-organic Frameworks
authors: Christopher M. Owen And Michael J. Lawler
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher M. Owen and Michael J. Lawler

Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) combine high porosity with structural fragility, raising important questions about their mechanical stability. We develop a rigidity-based formalism in which spring networks parameterized by universal force field for metal-organic frameworks are used to construct rigi…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014317] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the mechanical rigidity of metal-organic frameworks using spring network models.
motivation: Metal-organic frameworks combine high porosity with structural fragility, motivating a study of their mechanical stability.
method: A rigidity-based formalism is developed, parameterized by a universal force field, to construct and analyze spring networks.
result: The analysis identifies singularly isostatic and geometrically unstable rigidity regimes in these frameworks.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the mechanical stability of MOFs but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Environment-dependent Tight-binding Models From ab Initio Pseudoatomic Orbital Hamiltonians
authors: M. Buongiorno Nardelli
abstract:
Author(s): M. Buongiorno Nardelli

Ab initio pseudoatomic orbital (PAO) Hamiltonians express the electronic structure of a solid in a compact, localized basis that spans the same Hilbert space as a conventional Slater-Koster tight-binding model, thereby providing an exact ab initio representation without any loss of accuracy. Buildin…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045125] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to construct environment-dependent tight-binding models from ab initio pseudoatomic orbital Hamiltonians for accurate electronic structure calculations.
motivation: To bridge the gap between ab initio accuracy and tight-binding efficiency for large-scale simulations of solids.
method: The authors derive a mapping from ab initio pseudoatomic orbital Hamiltonians to a Slater-Koster tight-binding form, incorporating environment dependence through a self-consistent procedure.
result: The resulting tight-binding model reproduces the ab initio band structure and density of states with high accuracy for a range of materials.
conclusion: The approach provides a systematic way to generate accurate tight-binding models from first principles, enabling efficient simulations of complex materials.

title: Role Of Defect-induced Thermal Resistance In The Photoluminescence Intensity Of CVD-grown Monolayer $\mathrm{Mo}{\mathrm{S}}_{2}$: Short-term Aging Effects
authors: Akhil R Warrier, Kishore K. Madapu, And K. Prabakar
abstract:
Author(s): Akhil R Warrier, Kishore K. Madapu, and K. Prabakar

Two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) grown by chemical vapor deposition (CVD) have emerged as promising optoelectronic materials owing to their high optical quality and scalability. However, the stability and degradation of as-grown 2D TMDCs remain critical for realizing the…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055418] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies defect-induced thermal resistance and its effect on photoluminescence intensity in CVD-grown monolayer MoS2, focusing on short-term aging effects.
motivation: Understanding the stability and degradation of 2D TMDCs is critical for their optoelectronic applications, but the role of defects in thermal transport and photoluminescence is not well understood.
method: The authors investigate monolayer MoS2 grown by CVD, measuring photoluminescence intensity and correlating it with defect-induced thermal resistance through experiments and modeling.
result: They find that defect-induced thermal resistance significantly reduces photoluminescence intensity over short-term aging, indicating that thermal management is key to device performance.
conclusion: Defect engineering and thermal management are essential for improving the stability and performance of MoS2-based optoelectronic devices.

title: Voltage Characteristics Of Hydrodynamic Dirac Electron Nozzles With Supersonic Flow
authors: Kristof Moors, Oleksiy Kashuba, And Thomas L. Schmidt
abstract:
Author(s): Kristof Moors, Oleksiy Kashuba, and Thomas L. Schmidt

In clean Dirac electron systems such as graphene, electron-electron interactions can dominate over other relaxation mechanisms such as phonon or impurity scattering. In this limit, collective electron dynamics can be described by hydrodynamic equations. The prerequisites for electron hydrodynamics h…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055419] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies voltage characteristics of hydrodynamic electron nozzles with supersonic flow in graphene, focusing on electron hydrodynamics.
motivation: Understanding electron hydrodynamics in clean Dirac systems like graphene is important for describing collective electron dynamics when interactions dominate.
method: The authors use hydrodynamic equations to model electron flow and analyze voltage characteristics in nozzle geometries, considering supersonic flow regimes.
result: They derive voltage characteristics for Dirac electron nozzles under supersonic flow conditions, showing distinct features compared to subsonic flow.
conclusion: The work provides insights into electron hydrodynamics in graphene but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Highly Fluctuating Double-$q$ Magnetic Order In The Van Der Waals Metal ${\mathrm{CeTe}}_{3}$
authors: Ryutaro Okuma, Yuita Fujisawa, Natsumi Maekawa, Akiko Nakao, Yoshihisa Ishikawa, Riki Kobayashi, Yoshinori Okada, And Daichi Ueta
